digSites.tips: Four Peaks amethyst is the regional specialty — the mine is one of the only commercial amethyst operations in the US. Arizona turquoise (sleeping beauty, morenci) is also here.

digSites.name: Tucson Mineral & Fossil Co
digSites.summary: Tucson's year-round mineral and fossil shop — the city hosts the world's largest gem and mineral show every February, and this shop keeps the spirit going all year.
digSites.tips: If you can't make the February Tucson Gem & Mineral Show, this is the year-round alternative. Worldwide inventory at every price point. Ask about the back-room high-end cabinet specimens.

digSites.name: Sedona Crystal Vortex
digSites.summary: Sedona metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz clusters, Arizona selenite, cathedral crystals, and vortex-themed specimens — Sedona's new-age scene is unmatched.
digSites.tips: Sedona's vortex tourism makes this a well-stocked metaphysical stop. Cathedral quartz and selenite swords are the specialty. Real specimen quality alongside the spiritual inventory.

digSites.name: Wegner Quartz Crystal Mines (Shop)
digSites.summary: The shop at Wegner Quartz Crystal Mines — Arkansas quartz crystals straight from the Ouachita Mountains source, plus a fee-dig option on the property.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse. Fee-dig $20+ per person.
digSites.tips: Mine-direct Arkansas quartz — every piece came out of the Ouachita Mountains. The fee-dig at the tailings pile is the bargain; bring your own tools and dig your own crystals.

digSites.name: Mount Ida Crystal City
digSites.summary: Mount Ida — the 'Quartz Crystal Capital of the World' — has a row of rock shops along Highway 270 carrying mine-direct Arkansas quartz at every price point.
digSites.hours: Daily 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM (season varies by shop)
digSites.tips: Drive Highway 270 through Mount Ida and stop at any of the crystal shops. Prices are negotiable on big pieces. Ask for 'mine-run' for unsorted buckets at bulk rates.

digSites.name: Hot Springs Crystal Corner
digSites.summary: Hot Springs metaphysical crystal shop — Arkansas quartz clusters, selenite wands, and tumbled stones, all sourced from the surrounding Ouachita Mountains.
digSites.tips: Hot Springs is the gateway to the Ouachita quartz region. This shop has mine-direct Arkansas quartz at fair prices. The bathhouse row location makes it an easy stop.

digSites.name: Pala International / Pala Gems
digSites.summary: Pala International — the historic gem operation in San Diego County's pegmatite district, source of world-famous tourmaline, kunzite, and morganite from the Himalaya Mine.
digSites.tips: Pala is one of the most famous gem districts in North America. Tourmaline from the Himalaya Mine is the regional specialty. Call ahead — this is a working gem operation, not a retail shop.

digSites.name: Los Angeles Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: LA's full-service rock and fossil shop — California minerals, worldwide specimens, fossils, and a strong lapidary supply section.
digSites.tips: Ask about California benitoite — the state gem — from San Benito County. The fossil room is worth a walkthrough; trilobites and ammonites are well-represented.

digSites.name: Topanga Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Topanga Canyon metaphysical crystal shop — a curated selection of quartz, selenite, celestite, and tumbled stones in a rustic canyon setting.
digSites.tips: A classic Topanga new-age stop. Celestite geodes from Madagascar are the highlight. The canyon drive alone is worth the trip.

digSites.name: Big Sur Jade Company
digSites.summary: Big Sur jade shop carrying nephrite jade pebbles and carvings from the famous Big Sur and Monterey Bay beach jade deposits.
digSites.tips: Big Sur beach jade is the regional specialty — nephrite pebbles tumbled by the Pacific. Carvings and cabochons are made on-site. Combine with a jade-hunting walk on the coast.

digSites.name: Colorado Collector's Warehouse
digSites.summary: Golden shop specializing in Colorado minerals — rhodochrosite (the state mineral) from the Sweet Home Mine, amazonite and smoky quartz from the Pikes Peak batholith, and tellurides from the Cripple Creek district.
digSites.tips: Colorado rhodochrosite from the Sweet Home Mine is the prize — the finest in the world. Amazonite-smoky quartz combinations from Pikes Peak are the regional classic.

digSites.name: Alma Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Alma shop at the foot of Mount Bross — the local pegmatites produce amazonite, smoky quartz, topaz, and phenakite, all represented here alongside Colorado rhodochrosite.
digSites.tips: Alma is the gateway to the Mount Bross pegmatite district. Amazonite-smoky quartz combinations are the regional classic. Hours are seasonal — call ahead in winter.

digSites.name: Denver Crystal & Mineral
digSites.summary: Denver metaphysical crystal shop carrying Colorado amazonite, smoky quartz, selenite, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Metaphysical focus but the Colorado amazonite and smoky quartz are real specimens from the Pikes Peak pegmatites. The Denver Gem & Mineral Show in September is the big annual event.

digSites.name: Boulder Rock Shop
digSites.summary: Boulder's full-service rock shop — Colorado minerals, fossils, lapidary supplies, and a strong metaphysical crystal section.
digSites.tips: Boulder is the gateway to the Colorado Front Range pegmatites. Amazonite and smoky quartz from the local claims are well-stocked. The fossil section is worth a look too.

digSites.name: Mystic Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Mystic rock shop carrying Connecticut garnet, beryl, and Connecticut Valley fossils, plus a wide selection of tumbled stones and cabochons.
digSites.tips: Connecticut garnet from the Roxbury district is the regional specialty. The owner is a longtime collector and happy to share local site tips.

digSites.name: Hartford Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Hartford metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones with a calm, well-organized layout.
digSites.tips: Well-curated amethyst geodes and quartz clusters. The metaphysical selection is solid; the specimen quality is real. A calm stop in downtown Hartford.

digSites.name: Collins Hill Quarry Gift Shop
digSites.summary: Small shop near the historic Collins Hill quarry district carrying Connecticut pegmatite minerals — beryl, garnet, tourmaline — and local fossils.
digSites.tips: Weekend-only hours — call ahead. The Collins Hill pegmatites produced some of Connecticut's best beryl and tourmaline. Specimens from the old quarries are the specialty.

digSites.name: Rehoboth Rock & Shell
digSites.summary: Rehoboth Beach shop carrying Delaware Bay fossils, shark teeth, beach glass, and polished stones — a classic shore-town rock-and-shell shop.
digSites.tips: Beach glass and fossil shark teeth from the Delaware Bay are the regional draw. A fun shore-town stop — combine with a beachcombing walk at Cape Henlopen.

digSites.name: Wilmington Crystal & Mineral
digSites.summary: Wilmington metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: The only dedicated crystal shop in Delaware. Well-curated amethyst geodes and quartz clusters. The owner sources from the larger Tucson show each year.

digSites.name: Dover Mineral & Fossil
digSites.summary: Dover shop carrying Mid-Atlantic fossils, Delaware Bay shark teeth, and a small selection of regional minerals.
digSites.tips: Small but well-stocked with Mid-Atlantic fossils. The owner is a Delaware Bay fossil collector — ask about the best public beach access for shark-tooth hunting.

digSites.name: Venice Fossil & Shark Tooth
digSites.summary: Venice shop specializing in the local megalodon and fossil shark teeth — Venice is the 'Shark Tooth Capital of the World,' and this shop has the teeth to prove it.
digSites.tips: Megalodon teeth from the local beaches are the draw — sizes from half-inch to five-plus inches, every price point. Ask about the runner-up bucket for affordable smaller teeth.

digSites.name: Tampa Bay Fossil Hunting
digSites.summary: Tampa shop carrying Florida's famous Peace River fossils — megalodon teeth, mastodon teeth, dugong ribs, and fossilized coral.
digSites.tips: Peace River fossils are the regional specialty. The shop offers guided fossil-hunting trips on the river — a great way to find your own megalodon teeth.

digSites.name: Miami Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Miami metaphysical crystal shop — large quartz clusters, amethyst geodes, selenite towers, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Miami's largest metaphysical crystal shop. Selenite towers from Morocco are a specialty. The geode room is worth a walkthrough — some pieces are cabinet-grade.

digSites.name: Graves Mountain Rock Shop
digSites.summary: The shop at the famous Graves Mountain — world-class rutile, lazulite, pyrophyllite, and kyanite crystals from one of Georgia's most famous mineral localities.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse. Annual digs ($10–20) hosted by the mountain's caretaker club.
digSites.hours: By appointment; annual dig days in spring/fall
digSites.tips: Graves Mountain rutile is world-famous — the red prismatic crystals are some of the finest anywhere. The annual dig days are the only public collecting access; check the club schedule.

digSites.name: Atlanta Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Atlanta's full-service rock shop — Georgia minerals (rutile, kyanite, garnet), fossils, lapidary supplies, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Georgia garnet from the Piedmont is well-stocked. The lapidary supply section is one of the best in the Southeast — good for cabbing rough and polishing supplies.

digSites.name: Decatur Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Decatur metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz clusters, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone wall.
digSites.tips: Atlanta's metaphysical mainstay. The tumbled-stone wall is one of the widest selections in the Southeast. Selenite and quartz clusters are well-priced.

digSites.name: Big Island Rock Shop
digSites.summary: Hilo shop carrying Hawaiian olivine (peridot) sand, polished basalt, and Big Island volcanic specimens — the regional rockhound stop.
digSites.tips: Hawaiian olivine sand (the famous green sand) is the regional specialty. Peridot grains from the Big Island's volcanic fields are sold by the vial. Take only what you buy — beach collecting is restricted.

digSites.name: Honolulu Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Honolulu metaphysical crystal shop — Hawaiian olivine, quartz, amethyst, and tumbled stones in a relaxed island setting.
digSites.tips: Hawaiian olivine peridot is the local specialty. The shop imports the rest — quartz, amethyst, selenite — from the mainland. A good stop for island-themed crystal gifts.

digSites.name: Maui Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Maui shop carrying Hawaiian volcanic specimens, olivine sand, and a small fossil selection — a compact island rockhound stop.
digSites.tips: Small but well-stocked. Hawaiian volcanic specimens are the regional draw — olivine basalt, pumice, and peridot sand. Combine with a beach walk at the green sand beach.

digSites.name: Emerald Creek Garnet Shop
digSites.summary: The shop at the Emerald Creek garnet dig — Idaho star garnets (the state gem) straight from the source, plus a fee-dig option on the claim.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse. Fee-dig $15 per person.
digSites.tips: Idaho star garnets are found in only two places on Earth — Emerald Creek and India. The dig is the bargain; bring screens and a shovel. The shop sells polished star garnet cabochons.

digSites.name: Boise Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Boise's full-service rock shop — Idaho star garnets, jasper, agate, fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Idaho star garnet cabochons are the regional specialty — the four-ray and six-ray stars are unique. The jasper and agate selection comes from the Idaho Batholith gravels.

digSites.name: Coeur d'Alene Crystal Corner
digSites.summary: Coeur d'Alene metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection in North Idaho.
digSites.tips: A calm metaphysical stop in North Idaho. The owner stocks Idaho smoky quartz from the Idaho Batholith. Good selection of tumbled stones and selenite towers.

digSites.name: Cave-in Rock Minerals
digSites.summary: Shop at the famous Cave-in-Rock fluorite district — the world's finest fluorite crystals (purple, blue, yellow) plus calcite, galena, and witherite from the Illinois-Kentucky Fluorspar District.
digSites.tips: Cave-in-Rock fluorite is world-famous — the purple and blue cubic crystals are some of the finest anywhere. Ask about the local mine dumps; some allow collecting for a fee.

digSites.name: Chicago Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Chicago's full-service rock shop — Illinois fluorite, Mazon Creek fossils, Lake Michigan agates, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Mazon Creek fossils (Pennsylvanian-age ferns, jellyfish, Tullimonstrum) are Illinois' state fossil and a regional specialty. The fluorite selection comes from Cave-in-Rock.

digSites.name: Evanston Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Evanston metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz clusters, amethyst geodes, selenite, and tumbled stones near Northwestern University.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop just north of Chicago. Amethyst geodes from Brazil are a specialty. The owner is knowledgeable about crystal formation.

digSites.name: Bloomington Limestone & Fossil
digSites.summary: Bloomington shop carrying Indiana's famous Salem Limestone fossils — crinoids, brachiopods, and bryozoans — plus geodes and Indiana minerals.
digSites.tips: Indiana limestone is the state rock and full of Mississippian fossils. The shop sells polished fossil slabs and rough limestone with crinoid stems. Bring a small hand lens.

digSites.name: Indianapolis Rock Shop
digSites.summary: Indianapolis full-service rock shop — Indiana geodes, fossils, Harrodsburg limestone specimens, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Indiana geodes from the Harrodsburg area are the regional specialty — crack them open for quartz, calcite, and occasional pyrite. The lapidary supply section is well-stocked.

digSites.name: Bloomington Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Bloomington metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in a cozy college-town setting.
digSites.tips: A calm metaphysical stop in downtown Bloomington. Good selection of quartz clusters and amethyst geodes. The owner stocks Indiana geodes too.

digSites.name: Keokuk Geode Shop
digSites.summary: Keokuk shop at the heart of the famous Keokuk geode beds — geodes full of quartz, calcite, pyrite, and occasional rare minerals, sold whole or pre-cracked.
digSites.tips: Keokuk geodes are the regional specialty — the bed spans Iowa, Illinois, and Missouri. Buy them pre-cracked to see the crystals, or whole to crack yourself. The shop sells geode-cracking tools too.

digSites.name: Des Moines Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Des Moines full-service rock shop — Keokuk geodes, Iowa fossils, Lake Michigan agates in glacial drift, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: The geode selection comes straight from the Keokuk beds. Lake Michigan agates in glacial drift are the bonus find — the owner knows the local creek gravels.

digSites.name: Cedar Rapids Crystal Corner
digSites.summary: Cedar Rapids metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in eastern Iowa. The owner carries Keokuk geodes alongside the standard quartz and amethyst selection.

digSites.name: Niobrara Chalk & Fossil
digSites.summary: Hays shop specializing in the Niobrara Chalk fossils of western Kansas — mosasaurs, pteranodons, fossil fish, and the famous Kansas chalk formations.
digSites.tips: Western Kansas is one of the world's great Cretaceous fossil localities. The Sternberg Museum in Hays is a must-visit companion. The shop carries fossil fish plates and mosasaur teeth.

digSites.name: Wichita Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Wichita rock shop carrying Kansas septarian nodules, selenite, Niobrara chalk fossils, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Kansas septarian nodules are the regional specialty — crack them open for yellow calcite and aragonite. Selenite from the Kansas salt flats is also well-stocked.

digSites.name: Overland Park Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Overland Park metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in suburban Kansas City.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in the Kansas City suburbs. Amethyst geodes and quartz clusters are the specialty. The owner sources from the larger Tucson show each year.

digSites.name: Ben E. Clement Mineral Museum Shop
digSites.summary: Marion museum and shop at the heart of the Illinois-Kentucky Fluorspar District — world-class fluorite crystals, calcite, galena, and the famous Kentucky agate.
digSites.tips: The Clement collection is one of the finest fluorite collections in the world — Kentucky fluorite crystals in purple, blue, yellow, and the rare banded 'Blue Grass' fluorite. Kentucky agate is also here.

digSites.name: Louisville Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Louisville rock shop carrying Kentucky agate, fluorite, geodes, and Ohio Valley fossils.
digSites.tips: Kentucky agate (blue and gray banded) is the regional specialty. The fluorite comes from the Western Kentucky Fluorspar District. Crinoid fossils from the local limestone are common.

digSites.name: Lexington Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Lexington metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection in the heart of horse country.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop. The owner carries Kentucky agate alongside the standard crystal inventory — a nice regional touch.

digSites.name: Louisiana Agate & Fossil
digSites.summary: Alexandria shop carrying Louisiana agate, petrified wood from the Citronelle Formation, and Gulf Coast fossils.
digSites.tips: Louisiana agate from the Grant Parish gravels is the regional specialty — small but beautiful. Petrified wood from the Citronelle Formation is also well-represented.

digSites.name: New Orleans Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: New Orleans rock shop carrying Gulf Coast fossils, Louisiana agate, polished stones, and a wide tumbled-stone wall.
digSites.tips: Gulf Coast fossils — megalodon teeth, shell hash, chert — are the regional draw. The French Quarter location makes it an easy tourist stop. Combine with a beach walk at Grand Isle.

digSites.name: Baton Rouge Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Baton Rouge metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in Louisiana's capital.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Baton Rouge. Selenite towers and amethyst geodes are the specialty. The owner is knowledgeable about crystal formations.

digSites.name: Maine Mineral & Gem Museum Shop
digSites.summary: The shop at the Maine Mineral & Gem Museum — world-class Maine tourmaline, beryl, garnet, and amethyst from the famous New England pegmatites, plus the museum's meteorite collection.
digSites.tips: The museum is a must-visit — the Maine tourmaline collection is world-class, and the meteorite collection is the largest in New England. The shop sells Maine pegmatite specimens at every price point.

digSites.name: Paris Marble Quarry Shop
digSites.summary: South Paris shop at the historic Maine pegmatite district — tourmaline, beryl (morganite), garnet, and smoky quartz from the local quarries.
digSites.tips: South Paris is the heart of the Maine pegmatite district. The famous Mt. Mica tourmaline locality is nearby. Ask about mine-run lots for unsorted pegmatite material.

digSites.name: Portland Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Portland metaphysical crystal shop carrying Maine tourmaline, quartz, amethyst, and a curated tumbled-stone selection on the Maine coast.
digSites.tips: Maine tourmaline (watermelon, elbaite) is the regional specialty. The owner sources from the New England pegmatites. A nice stop on a Portland walking tour.

digSites.name: Baltimore Mineral Society Shop
digSites.summary: Baltimore rock shop carrying Maryland minerals (Patuxent agate, serpentine), Chesapeake Miocene fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Patuxent agate from Maryland's coastal plain is the regional specialty. Chesapeake Miocene fossils — Chesapecten scallops, shark teeth — are also well-stocked. Combine with a trip to Calvert Cliffs.

digSites.name: Calvert Cliffs Fossil Shop
digSites.summary: Lusby shop near Calvert Cliffs State Park — Miocene fossils (shark teeth, whale bones, Chesapecten scallops) straight from the Chesapeake cliffs.
digSites.tips: Calvert Cliffs is one of the East Coast's best Miocene fossil localities. The shop sells megalodon teeth, Chesapecten (Maryland's state fossil), and fossilized whale bone fragments.

digSites.name: Silver Spring Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Silver Spring metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in the DC suburbs.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop just north of DC. The owner sources from the larger Tucson show. Amethyst geodes and selenite towers are the specialty.

digSites.name: Boston Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Boston rock shop carrying New England pegmatite minerals (tourmaline, beryl, garnet), Cape Cod beach pebbles, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: New England pegmatite minerals are the regional specialty — Maine tourmaline, New Hampshire beryl, Massachusetts garnet. The lapidary supply section is one of the best in New England.

digSites.name: Cambridge Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Cambridge metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones near Harvard Square.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop near Harvard. The owner is a former geologist — happy to discuss crystal formation. Amethyst geodes are the specialty.

digSites.name: Greenfield Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Greenfield shop carrying New England minerals, Connecticut Valley fossils, and the famous Bernardston radiolarian fossils.
digSites.tips: The Bernardston radiolarian fossils are a regional specialty — tiny Cambrian microfossils in chert. Bring a hand lens. The owner knows the local collecting sites.

digSites.name: A.E. Seaman Mineral Museum Shop
digSites.summary: The shop at the A.E. Seaman Mineral Museum on the Michigan Tech campus — world-class Keweenaw minerals: native copper, datolite, chlorastrolite (the state gem), prehnite, and thomsonite.
digSites.tips: The Seaman Museum is the official Michigan mineral museum — the Keweenaw mineral collection is world-class. The shop sells chlorastrolite (Michigan's state gem), datolite nodules, and native copper specimens.

digSites.name: Keweenaw Rock & Gift
digSites.summary: Calumet shop at the heart of the Keweenaw copper country — native copper, datolite, chlorastrolite, thomsonite, and Yooperlite specimens from the local beaches and mines.
digSites.tips: Native copper specimens from the Keweenaw mines are the regional specialty — crystallized copper is the prize. Yooperlite (UV-fluorescent sodalite syenite) is the modern must-have. Ask about UV flashlights.

digSites.name: Petoskey Stone & Fossil
digSites.summary: Petoskey shop specializing in Michigan's state stone — polished Petoskey and Charlevoix stones, fossil coral, and Lake Michigan beach finds.
digSites.tips: Petoskey and Charlevoix stones are the regional specialty — polished cabs and raw beach pebbles. The shop sells polishing kits so you can finish your own beach finds.

digSites.name: Detroit Rock Shop
digSites.summary: Detroit's full-service rock shop — Petoskey and Charlevoix stones, Lake Superior agates, Michigan minerals, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Detroit's best rock shop. Petoskey and Charlevoix stones from up north, Lake Superior agates, and the full lapidary supply corner. Good for rock-tumbling rough and polishing supplies.

digSites.name: Quincy Mine Gift Shop
digSites.summary: The gift shop at the Quincy Mine & Hoist Association — native copper specimens, datolite nodules, calcite crystals from the Quincy mine workings, plus books and Keweenaw souvenirs. The Quincy Mine produced some of the finest crystallized native copper ever found.
digSites.tips: The Quincy Mine produced world-class crystallized native copper — ask about the copper crystal specimens. The shop carries genuine Quincy mine copper and datolite nodules you won't find anywhere else. Take the underground tour for context on the deepest shaft in the Keweenaw.

digSites.name: Prospector's Paradise
digSites.summary: Allouez rock shop in the heart of Keweenaw copper country — native copper, datolite, prehnite, Mohawkite, and Lake Superior agates from the nearby Mohawk and Iroquois mine dumps. A must-stop for collectors working the Allouez–Mohawk district.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse. Specimens priced by weight and quality.
digSites.hours: Mon–Sat 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM (Jun–Oct); call for off-season hours
digSites.tips: The Allouez–Mohawk district is the only place on Earth to find Mohawkite — ask about specimens with white quartz matrix. The shop stocks datolite nodules in every color from the local mine dumps. Bring a UV light — some local datolite fluoresces.

digSites.name: Ann Arbor Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Ann Arbor metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones near the University of Michigan.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in downtown Ann Arbor. The owner stocks Lake Superior agates and Petoskey stones alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Lake Superior Agate Shop
digSites.summary: Duluth shop specializing in Minnesota's state gemstone — Lake Superior agates with rich red and orange banding, plus thomsonite pebbles from the North Shore.
digSites.tips: Lake Superior agates are the regional specialty — the state gem, with rich iron-red banding. Thomsonite pebbles with pink 'eyes' are the bonus find. The shop sells agate-hunting kits with a UV light.

digSites.name: Minneapolis Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Minneapolis full-service rock shop — Lake Superior agates, Minnesota minerals, fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Lake Superior agates in every size and price point. The lapidary supply section is one of the best in the Upper Midwest — good for cabbing rough and polishing supplies.

digSites.name: St. Paul Crystal Corner
digSites.summary: St. Paul metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a wide tumbled-stone selection in the Twin Cities.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in St. Paul. The owner carries Lake Superior agates alongside the standard crystal inventory — a nice regional touch.

digSites.name: Jackson Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Jackson rock shop carrying Mississippi fossils (Cretaceous chalk fossils, shark teeth), petrified wood, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Mississippi's Cretaceous chalk fossils are the regional specialty — the state has rich fossil-bearing deposits. Petrified wood from the Catahoula Formation is also well-represented.

digSites.name: Gulfport Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Gulfport metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones on the Mississippi Gulf Coast.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop on the Mississippi coast. The owner stocks Gulf Coast fossils — megalodon teeth, shell hash — alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Vicksburg Fossil & Mineral
digSites.summary: Vicksburg shop carrying Mississippi loess fossils, Cretaceous chalk fossils, and a small selection of regional minerals.
digSites.tips: Mississippi loess fossils (Pleistocene land snails, vertebrate bones) are a regional specialty. The Vicksburg bluffs are famous for fossil-bearing loess deposits.

digSites.name: Branson Rock Shop & Mine
digSites.summary: Branson shop with on-site mining — Mozarkite (the state rock), drusy quartz, galena, crinoid fossils, and a fee-dig sluice on the property.
digSites.tips: Mozarkite is Missouri's state rock — a colorful chert with swirls of pink, gray, and tan. The sluice is a fun family activity; buckets come pre-loaded with rough.

digSites.name: Kansas City Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Kansas City full-service rock shop — Mozarkite, geodes, Missouri fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Mozarkite cabs and rough are the regional specialty. The geode selection comes from the Keokuk district just across the Iowa border. Good lapidary supply section.

digSites.name: St. Louis Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: St. Louis metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in St. Louis. The owner carries Missouri Mozarkite and Keokuk geodes alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Yogo Sapphire Shop
digSites.summary: Utica shop at the famous Yogo Gulch sapphire deposit — natural Yogo sapphires (the cornflower-blue Montana state gem), cut stones, and rough.
digSites.tips: Yogo sapphires are among the finest natural sapphires in the world — the cornflower blue is unique. Hours are seasonal; call ahead in winter. The shop sells cut stones and rough.

digSites.name: Butte Mineral & Gem
digSites.summary: Butte shop at the famous copper mining district — Montana copper minerals, sapphires, moss agate, and the famous Butte rhodochrosite.
digSites.tips: Butte is one of the most famous mining districts in the world. The copper minerals (bornite, chrysocolla, native copper) are regional classics. Montana moss agate and sapphire too.

digSites.name: Missoula Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Missoula metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection in western Montana.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Missoula. The owner carries Montana moss agate and sapphire alongside the standard crystal inventory — a nice regional touch.

digSites.name: Blue River Agate & Fossil
digSites.summary: Lincoln shop carrying Nebraska's Blue Chalcedony, Platte River agates, and the famous Ogallala Formation fossil teeth.
digSites.tips: Nebraska Blue Chalcedony is the regional specialty — a soft blue translucent chalcedony. Fossil mastodon and horse teeth from the Ogallala Formation are the bonus find.

digSites.name: Omaha Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Omaha full-service rock shop — Nebraska agates, fossils, Lake Superior agates in glacial drift, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Lake Superior agates in glacial drift are the bonus find — the glaciers carried them south. The owner knows the local creek gravels.

digSites.name: Lincoln Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Lincoln metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Lincoln. The owner stocks Nebraska Blue Chalcedony alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Turquoise King
digSites.summary: Las Vegas shop specializing in Nevada turquoise — the famous Royston, Carico Lake, and Number 8 mines — plus opal and Nevada minerals.
digSites.tips: Nevada turquoise is among the finest in the world — Royston (green-blue), Carico Lake (lime green), and Number 8 (webbed) are the famous mines. The shop sells cabs and rough.

digSites.name: Reno Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Reno full-service rock shop — Nevada turquoise, Black Rock Desert opal, petrified wood, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Nevada turquoise and the famous Virgin Valley opal (black opal from the northern Nevada diggings) are the regional specialties. Good lapidary supply section.

digSites.name: Carson City Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Carson City metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection in Nevada's capital.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Carson City. The owner carries Nevada turquoise and Virgin Valley opal alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Palermo Mine Shop
digSites.summary: Groton shop at the famous Palermo pegmatite — one of the world's most mineralogically diverse pegmatites, with over 150 minerals including the rare palermoite.
digSites.tips: Palermo is one of the world's great phosphate mineral localities — over 150 minerals. Call ahead — this is a working claim, not a retail shop. Beryl and garnet are the common prizes.

digSites.name: North Conway Rock Shop
digSites.summary: North Conway rock shop carrying New Hampshire pegmatite minerals — smoky quartz, beryl, garnet, topaz — and White Mountain fossils.
digSites.tips: New Hampshire smoky quartz from the Conway granite is the regional specialty — some of the darkest, most lustrous smoky quartz in the world. Beryl and topaz from the local pegmatites too.

digSites.name: Keene Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Keene metaphysical crystal shop carrying New Hampshire smoky quartz, beryl, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Keene. The owner sources smoky quartz from the local Conway granite — some of the finest smoky quartz in the world.

digSites.name: Franklin Mineral Museum Shop
digSites.summary: The shop at the Franklin Mineral Museum — Franklin is the 'Fluorescent Mineral Capital of the World,' with over 90 fluorescent mineral species found only here.
digSites.tips: Franklin is the world's most famous fluorescent mineral locality — willemite glows green, calcite glows red under UV. The shop sells UV lights and fluorescent specimen kits. A must-visit.

digSites.name: Sterling Hill Mining Museum Shop
digSites.summary: Sterling Hill Mining Museum shop — the second of Franklin's two famous fluorescent mineral mines, with over 350 minerals found on the property.
digSites.tips: Sterling Hill is the partner locality to Franklin — over 350 minerals, including 90+ fluorescent species. The mine tour is excellent; the dump collecting area lets you take home your own fluorescent specimens.

digSites.name: Cape May Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Cape May shop carrying the famous 'Cape May Diamonds' (clear quartz pebbles from the Delaware Bay), jasper, agate, and beach glass.
digSites.tips: Cape May Diamonds are the regional specialty — clear quartz pebbles tumbled by the Delaware Bay that look like waterworn diamonds. The shop sells polished specimens and jewelry.

digSites.name: Turquoise Museum Shop
digSites.summary: Albuquerque's Turquoise Museum shop — the world's premier turquoise collection, with specimens from every major US turquoise mine (Cerrillos, Sleeping Beauty, Morenci, Kingman).
digSites.tips: The Turquoise Museum is a must-visit for turquoise collectors — specimens from every major US mine, with the famous Cerrillos (New Mexico's historic turquoise district) well-represented.

digSites.name: Santa Fe Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Santa Fe rock shop carrying New Mexico turquoise, azurite, malachite, and a strong selection of Southwestern minerals and fossils.
digSites.tips: New Mexico turquoise and copper minerals (azurite, malachite) are the regional specialties. The Cerrillos district just south of Santa Fe is the historic turquoise source.

digSites.name: Albuquerque Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Albuquerque metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a wide tumbled-stone selection with a strong Southwestern focus.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Albuquerque. The owner carries New Mexico turquoise alongside the standard crystal inventory — a strong regional focus.

digSites.name: Herkimer Diamond Mines Shop
digSites.summary: Herkimer shop at the famous Herkimer diamond mines — doubly-terminated quartz crystals (Herkimer 'diamonds') straight from the source, plus a fee-dig on the property.
digSites.tips: Herkimer diamonds are the regional specialty — doubly-terminated quartz crystals with brilliant clarity. The fee-dig is the bargain; bring your own hammer and chisel.

digSites.name: New York Rock & Crystal
digSites.summary: NYC rock shop carrying worldwide minerals, Herkimer diamonds, New York garnet, and a wide lapidary supply selection.
digSites.tips: NYC's best rock shop. Herkimer diamonds and New York garnet (Barton Mine in the Adirondacks) are the regional specialties. The worldwide mineral selection is excellent.

digSites.name: Rochester Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Rochester metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection in western New York.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Rochester. The owner carries Herkimer diamonds from the nearby Mohawk Valley alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Spruce Pine Mineral Shop
digSites.summary: Spruce Pine shop at the heart of the famous Blue Ridge pegmatite district — emerald, aquamarine, morganite, tourmaline, and the famous Crabtree emerald mine specimens.
digSites.tips: Spruce Pine is one of the most famous pegmatite districts in North America — the source of the world's purest quartz (used in semiconductors). Emerald, aquamarine, and tourmaline are the regional specialties.

digSites.name: Asheville Rock & Crystal
digSites.summary: Asheville rock shop carrying North Carolina minerals (emerald, garnet, mica), Blue Ridge pegmatite specimens, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: North Carolina emerald from the Crabtree Mine is the regional specialty — the state gem. Garnet and mica from the Blue Ridge pegmatites are also well-represented.

digSites.name: Franklin Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Franklin rock shop carrying North Carolina rubies and sapphires from the Cowee Valley, plus fossils and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Franklin is the gateway to the Cowee Valley ruby and sapphire digs. The shop sells Cowee rubies and sapphires, plus polishing kits for the rough you find at the local fee-digs.

digSites.name: Petrified Wood Park Shop
digSites.summary: Lemmon shop near the ND/SD border carrying North Dakota petrified wood — the Cannonball Formation 'Teredo-bored' petrified wood and the famous Sentinel Butte petrified wood.
digSites.tips: North Dakota's petrified wood is the regional specialty — the 'Teredo-bored' variety (with shipworm holes) is unique to the Cannonball Formation. The Petrified Wood Park in Lemmon is a must-visit.

digSites.name: Fargo Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Fargo rock shop carrying North Dakota petrified wood, Lake Agassiz fossils, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Lake Agassiz fossils (Pleistocene lake deposits) and North Dakota petrified wood are the regional specialties. The owner knows the best public collecting spots in the state.

digSites.name: Bismarck Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Bismarck metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Bismarck. The owner stocks North Dakota petrified wood alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Flint Ridge Museum & Shop
digSites.summary: Flint Ridge shop at the famous Flint Ridge flint locality — Ohio's state gemstone, with kaleidoscopic colors from red and blue to pink and yellow.
digSites.tips: Flint Ridge flint is Ohio's state gemstone — one of the most colorful flints in the world, used by Native Americans for over 12,000 years. The shop sells raw flint and knapped points.

digSites.name: Cleveland Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Cleveland full-service rock shop — Ohio flint, Lake Erie fossils (Devonian horn coral, crinoid stems), and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Lake Erie Devonian fossils are the regional specialty — horn coral, crinoid stems, and brachiopods weather out of the shale bluffs. Flint Ridge flint is the bonus.

digSites.name: Columbus Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Columbus metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Columbus. The owner carries Flint Ridge flint alongside the standard crystal inventory — a nice regional touch.

digSites.name: Barite Rose Shop
digSites.summary: Noble shop specializing in the Oklahoma 'barite rose' — the state rock, sand-barite crystals shaped like rose petals, found only in Oklahoma.
digSites.tips: Barite roses are Oklahoma's state rock — sand-barite crystals shaped like rose petals, found only in a few Oklahoma counties. The shop sells single roses, clusters, and polished specimens.

digSites.name: Oklahoma City Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: OKC rock shop carrying barite roses, Oklahoma fossils (Permian reptiles), selenite, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Oklahoma barite roses are the regional specialty. The Permian red beds produce reptile fossils — the state's fossil heritage. Selenite from the Great Salt Plains is also well-stocked.

digSites.name: Tulsa Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Tulsa metaphysical crystal shop carrying quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Tulsa. The owner carries Oklahoma barite roses and Great Salt Plains selenite alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Prineville Thunderegg Shop
digSites.summary: Prineville shop at the heart of Oregon's thunderegg country — the state rock, geode-like nodules filled with agate, jasper, opal, and quartz.
digSites.tips: Thundereggs are Oregon's state rock — geode-like nodules with agate, jasper, and opal centers. The shop sells uncut eggs (crack your own) and cut-and-polished halves.

digSites.name: Portland Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Portland full-service rock shop — Oregon thundereggs, agates, jasper, sunstones (the state gem), and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Oregon sunstone (the state gem) from the Plush digs is a regional specialty — a feldspar with copper schiller. Thundereggs and beach agates from the Oregon coast too.

digSites.name: Eugene Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Eugene metaphysical crystal shop carrying Oregon sunstone, quartz, amethyst, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Eugene. The owner carries Oregon sunstone and thundereggs alongside the standard crystal inventory — a strong regional focus.

digSites.name: Pittsburgh Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Pittsburgh rock shop carrying Pennsylvania minerals (pyrite, quartz, fossils), and a wide lapidary supply selection.
digSites.tips: Pennsylvania pyrite from the coal region is the regional specialty — sharp cubic crystals. The fossil selection includes Pennsylvanian-age plant fossils from the coal measures.

digSites.name: Philadelphia Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Philadelphia rock shop carrying Pennsylvania minerals, fossils, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A solid East Coast rock shop. The owner stocks Pennsylvania pyrite and fossils alongside a wide tumbled-stone wall. Good for cabbing rough.

digSites.name: Philadelphia Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Philadelphia metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Philadelphia. Amethyst geodes and selenite towers are the specialty.

digSites.name: Providence Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Providence rock shop carrying Rhode Island minerals (Cumberlandite — the state rock), beach pebbles from Block Island, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: Cumberlandite is Rhode Island's state rock — a rare titaniferous magnetite found only in Cumberland. The shop sells specimens and polished cabs.

digSites.name: Newport Fossil & Crystal
digSites.summary: Newport shop carrying Rhode Island beach pebbles, fossils, and a small crystal selection.
digSites.tips: Newport's ocean-side location makes it a natural stop for beach-pebble collectors. The shop sells polished stones from the local shores.

digSites.name: Providence Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Providence metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in Rhode Island's capital.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Providence. The owner stocks Cumberlandite and beach pebbles alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Abbeville Amethyst Shop
digSites.summary: Abbeville shop at the heart of South Carolina's amethyst district — local amethyst crystals from the Piedmont pegmatites.
digSites.tips: South Carolina amethyst from the Abbeville County pegmatites is the regional specialty — pale to medium purple crystals in quartz veins. The owner knows the local dig sites.

digSites.name: Charleston Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Charleston rock shop carrying South Carolina fossils (Miocene phosphate bed fossils, shark teeth), amethyst, and tumbled stones.
digSites.tips: Charleston's phosphate beds produce world-class Miocene fossils — megalodon teeth, whale bones. The shop sells amethyst from the upstate alongside the coastal fossils.

digSites.name: Columbia Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Columbia metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in South Carolina's capital.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Columbia. The owner carries South Carolina amethyst from the Abbeville district alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Fairburn Agate Shop
digSites.summary: Fairburn shop at the type locality for the Fairburn agate — South Dakota's state gemstone, with the most intricate fortification banding of any agate.
digSites.tips: Fairburn agates are SD's state gem — intricate fortification banding in red, orange, pink, yellow, black, and white. The best specimens sell for thousands. Ask about mine-run lots for unsorted material.

digSites.name: Keystone Rock & Gift
digSites.summary: Keystone shop in the Black Hills carrying Fairburn agates, prairie agates, Black Hills fossils, and a wide gift selection.
digSites.tips: Keystone is the tourist gateway to Mount Rushmore and a great stop for Fairburn agates. The Black Hills also produce prairie agates and fossils. Watch for tourist-trap pricing — shop around.

digSites.name: Rapid City Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Rapid City metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection in the Black Hills.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Rapid City. The owner carries Fairburn agates and Black Hills minerals alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Tennessee Agate Shop
digSites.summary: McMinnville shop specializing in Tennessee agate — blue-banded, paint agate, and the famous Tennessee 'Hillbilly' agate from the Cumberland Plateau.
digSites.tips: Tennessee agate (blue-banded, paint) is the regional specialty — some of the most distinctive banding in the US. The owner knows the local Cumberland Plateau dig sites.

digSites.name: Nashville Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Nashville rock shop carrying Tennessee agate, fluorite, fossils (Mississippian crinoids), and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Tennessee agate and the famous Central Tennessee fluorite (purple, yellow) are the regional specialties. Mississippian crinoid fossils from the local limestone are common.

digSites.name: Memphis Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Memphis metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in western Tennessee.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Memphis. The owner carries Tennessee agate alongside the standard crystal inventory — a nice regional touch.

digSites.name: Terlingua Agate Shop
digSites.summary: Terlingua shop at the famous West Texas agate district — Terlingua agate (colorful banded), Texas red plume agate, and the famous Big Bend agates.
digSites.tips: Terlingua is the heart of the West Texas agate country. The local agates — colorful banded, plume, and moss — are world-famous. Summer is brutal; visit October through April.

digSites.name: Austin Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Austin full-service rock shop — Texas agates, Llano area minerals (topaz, garnet), fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Texas topaz (the state gem) from the Llano Uplift is the regional specialty — colorless to pale blue crystals. Texas agates from the Big Bend are also well-stocked.

digSites.name: Houston Crystal & Gem
digSites.summary: Houston metaphysical crystal shop — large quartz clusters, amethyst geodes, selenite towers, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Houston's largest metaphysical crystal shop. Selenite towers and amethyst geodes are the specialty. The owner sources from the larger Tucson show each year.

digSites.name: Dugway Geode Shop
digSites.summary: Dugway shop at the famous Dugway geode beds — geodes filled with clear quartz, amethyst, and chalcedony, sold whole or pre-cracked.
digSites.tips: Dugway geodes are the regional specialty — geodes with clear quartz, amethyst, and chalcedony centers. The BLM claim is open to collecting; bring a shovel and a heavy hammer.

digSites.name: Salt Lake Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Salt Lake City full-service rock shop — Dugway geodes, topaz (Utah's state gem), red beryl, variscite, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Utah topaz (the state gem, from Topaz Mountain) and red beryl (the rarest beryl, from the Wah Wah Mountains) are the regional specialties. Variscite from the Lucin district too.

digSites.name: Provo Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Provo metaphysical crystal shop carrying Utah topaz, quartz, amethyst, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Provo. The owner carries Utah topaz and Dugway geodes alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Vermont Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Burlington rock shop carrying Vermont minerals (grossular garnet, the state gem), Champlain Valley fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Vermont grossular garnet (the state gem) from the Belvidere Mountain quarries is the regional specialty — cinnamon-brown to green crystals. Champlain Valley trilobites too.

digSites.name: Montpelier Rock Shop
digSites.summary: Montpelier rock shop carrying Vermont minerals, granite specimens (the state rock), and fossils.
digSites.tips: Barre granite (Vermont's state rock) from the famous Barre quarries is the regional specialty — used in monuments worldwide. Garnet from the Green Mountains too.

digSites.name: Burlington Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Burlington metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones on Lake Champlain.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop on the Burlington waterfront. The owner carries Vermont garnet and Champlain Valley fossils alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Virginia Gold-Pyrite Shop
digSites.summary: Goochland shop at the historic Virginia gold-pyrite belt — gold in quartz, pyrite cubes, and Virginia minerals from the old mine district.
digSites.tips: Virginia's gold-pyrite belt runs from just north of Richmond to the Blue Ridge. Gold in quartz and sharp pyrite cubes are the regional specialties. The owner knows the local mine dumps.

digSites.name: Richmond Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Richmond rock shop carrying Virginia minerals (gold, pyrite, amazonite), Piedmont fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Virginia amazonite from the Morefield Mine is the regional specialty — blue-green feldspar from the Amelia pegmatite. Gold-pyrite belt specimens and Piedmont fossils too.

digSites.name: Arlington Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Arlington metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in the DC suburbs.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Arlington. The owner carries Virginia amazonite and pyrite alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Seattle Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Seattle full-service rock shop — Washington minerals (opal, carnelian, jade), fossils, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Washington minerals are the regional specialty — opal from the Whidbey Island digs, carnelian from the Olympic beaches, and jade from the Cascades. Good lapidary supply section.

digSites.name: Tacoma Rock & Fossil
digSites.summary: Tacoma rock shop carrying Washington minerals, fossils (Miocene marine fossils from the coast), and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Washington's coast produces Miocene marine fossils — whale bones, fossil shells. The shop sells agates and carnelian from the Olympic beaches too.

digSites.name: Seattle Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Seattle metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Seattle. The owner carries Washington opal and Olympic beach agates alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: New River Gorge Fossil Shop
digSites.summary: Fayetteville shop carrying West Virginia fossils (Pennsylvanian plant fossils, ferns, calamites), corundum, and a small mineral selection.
digSites.tips: Pennsylvanian plant fossils (ferns, calamites, lepidodendron bark) from the New River Gorge coal measures are the regional specialty. The owner knows the local road cuts.

digSites.name: Charleston Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Charleston rock shop carrying West Virginia fossils, corundum, geodes, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: West Virginia corundum from the Greenbrier region is the regional specialty. Pennsylvanian plant fossils from the coal measures are the bonus. Good lapidary supply section.

digSites.name: Morgantown Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Morgantown metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in northern West Virginia.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Morgantown. The owner carries West Virginia plant fossils and corundum alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Eau Claire Agate Shop
digSites.summary: Eau Claire shop carrying Wisconsin's Lake Superior agates (the state gem), Prairie du Chien fossils, and a wide tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: Lake Superior agates in glacial drift are the regional specialty — Wisconsin is one of the southernmost states where they wash up. Prairie du Chien fossils too.

digSites.name: Milwaukee Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Milwaukee full-service rock shop — Lake Superior agates, Wisconsin fossils, minerals, and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Lake Superior agates are the regional specialty — the state gem, with rich red banding. The lapidary supply section is one of the best in Wisconsin.

digSites.name: Madison Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Madison metaphysical crystal shop — quartz, amethyst, selenite, and tumbled stones in Wisconsin's capital.
digSites.tips: A well-stocked metaphysical stop in Madison. The owner carries Lake Superior agates alongside the standard crystal inventory.

digSites.name: Wyoming Jade Shop
digSites.summary: Lander shop specializing in Wyoming jade (nephrite) — the state gem, from the famous Granite Mountains jade deposits, plus iolite and diamond fragments.
digSites.tips: Wyoming jade is the state gem — some of the finest nephrite in the world, in green, white, and lavender. Iolite from the Laramie Range and diamond fragments from the State Line district too.

digSites.name: Casper Rock & Mineral
digSites.summary: Casper rock shop carrying Wyoming jade, fossils (Green River Formation fish fossils), and lapidary supplies.
digSites.tips: Wyoming jade and Green River Formation fish fossils (from the famous Kemmerer deposits just over the border) are the regional specialties. The lapidary section is well-stocked for jade carving.

digSites.name: Jackson Crystal Cottage
digSites.summary: Jackson metaphysical crystal shop carrying Wyoming jade, quartz, amethyst, and a curated tumbled-stone selection.
digSites.tips: A well-curated metaphysical stop in Jackson. The owner carries Wyoming jade alongside the standard crystal inventory — a strong regional focus. A nice stop on a Teton trip.

digSites.name: Coober Pedy Opal Fields
digSites.summary: The opal capital of the world. This remote outback town produces over 70% of the world's precious opal. Several mines offer public fossicking and noodling (sorting through old mine tailings).
digSites.feeInfo: Free noodling on designated public areas. Mine tours $20–40 AUD.
digSites.tips: Noodling (sorting through old mine dumps) is free and productive. Bring a UV light — some Coober Pedy opals fluoresce. Visit the underground homes and churches dug into the rock.

digSites.name: Lightning Ridge Black Opal Mines
digSites.summary: The only source of true black opal — the rarest and most valuable opal in the world. Public fossicking areas and several working mines welcome visitors.
digSites.feeInfo: Fossicking permit $5 AUD. Mine tours $25–50 AUD.
digSites.tips: The public fossicking area at the 3-Mile field is most productive. Bring a small pick and sieve. Black opal shows its colors against a dark potch background — look for flashes of red and green.

digSites.name: Central Queensland Sapphire Gemfields
digSites.summary: One of the richest sapphire fields in the world. Multiple public fossicking areas and commercial mines where you can wash gravel for blue, green, and parti-colored sapphires.
digSites.feeInfo: Free public fossicking areas. Commercial mines $20–50 AUD.
digSites.tips: Screen wash the gravel from shallow pits near the creeks. The sapphires here are often parti-colored (blue and yellow in the same stone). A fossicking license is required but inexpensive.

digSites.name: The Crystal Cave
digSites.summary: Australia's most spectacular crystal shop and museum. Walk-through amethyst cave, giant geodes, and a stunning collection of Australian and worldwide minerals.
digSites.feeInfo: Museum entry $15 AUD. Shop free to browse.
digSites.tips: The walk-through amethyst geode is a must-see. Great selection of Australian opal and sapphire specimens for sale.

digSites.name: Mineral World & Fossicking Park
digSites.summary: A family-friendly mineral museum and shop with fossicking areas where visitors can search for their own gemstones in salted gravel beds.
digSites.tips: Great for families — kids love the guaranteed-find fossicking bags. The South Australian mineral collection is excellent.

digSites.name: Bancroft Mineral Collecting Area
digSites.summary: The 'Mineral Capital of Canada.' Numerous old mine dumps and road cuts yield apatite, beryl, tourmaline, garnet, and over 100 other mineral species.
digSites.feeInfo: Free on public collecting sites. Some private sites charge $10–20 CAD.
digSites.tips: The Princess Sodalite Quarry and the Bear Lake Diggings are the most productive public sites. Pick up a collecting map from the Bancroft visitor center.

digSites.name: Thunder Bay Amethyst Mines
digSites.summary: The amethyst capital of North America. Several mines produce distinctive deep purple amethyst with red hematite inclusions. Public digging available.
digSites.feeInfo: Pay per pound collected: $3–5 CAD/lb. Mine tours available.
digSites.tips: Thunder Bay amethyst is unique — the red hematite inclusions inside the purple crystals create a distinctive look. Bring a bucket and small hand tools.

digSites.name: Bay of Fundy Mineral Beaches
digSites.summary: The world's highest tides expose zeolites, agates, and Jurassic-aged fossils along the dramatic Bay of Fundy shoreline. A UNESCO Geopark.
digSites.feeInfo: Free on public beaches. Check tide tables — essential for safety.
digSites.hours: Daylight hours — go at low tide only
digSites.tips: The tides rise up to 50 feet — never get caught below the cliffs at rising tide. Look for zeolite-filled cavities in the basalt cliffs and agates on the beach.

digSites.name: Royal Ontario Museum Gem Gallery
digSites.summary: Canada's premier natural history museum with one of the country's finest gem and mineral galleries. Gift shop carries Canadian minerals.
digSites.feeInfo: Museum admission $23 CAD adults. Shop free with admission.
digSites.tips: The gallery features a spectacular Canadian amethyst geode and specimens from the Bancroft area. Great gift shop for Canadian mineral souvenirs.

digSites.name: Blue John Cavern
digSites.summary: The only source of Blue John — a rare blue-purple banded fluorite mined in the Peak District for over 200 years. Underground tours and mineral shop.
digSites.feeInfo: Cave tour £12 adults. Shop free to browse.
digSites.tips: Blue John is one of Britain's rarest minerals — only a few hundred pounds are mined each year. The underground tours are spectacular and the shop sells authentic Blue John jewelry.

digSites.name: Whitby Jet Beaches
digSites.summary: The historic source of Whitby Jet — black fossilized monkey-puzzle tree resin prized by Victorian mourners. Search the beaches after storms.
digSites.hours: Daylight hours — best after winter storms
digSites.tips: Look for lightweight black pieces among the beach pebbles — jet feels warm to the touch and leaves a brown streak. Whitby is also famous for ammonite fossils on the same beaches.

digSites.name: Newborough Beach Agate & Jasper Area
digSites.summary: The beaches of Anglesey yield colorful agates, jaspers, and beach-pebbled semi-precious stones among the dramatic Welsh coastline.
digSites.tips: Walk the beach at low tide. Look for waxy, translucent pebbles with banding — these are agates weathered from the local volcanic rocks.

digSites.name: Natural History Museum Mineral Gallery
digSites.summary: One of the world's finest mineral and gem collections, including the legendary Aurora Pyramid of Hope and world-class British mineral specimens.
digSites.tips: The mineral gallery is in the Red Zone. Don't miss the 9,381-carat Devonshire Emerald and the unique Blue John specimens from Derbyshire.

digSites.name: Idar-Oberstein Gem Center
digSites.summary: The historic gem-cutting capital of Europe. Home to German agate mines, the German Gemstone Museum, and hundreds of gemstone shops and cutters.
digSites.hours: Museum Tue–Sun 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM. Shops vary.
digSites.tips: Visit the historic agate mines carved into the hillside. The town has been cutting gems for over 500 years — the selection of cut stones is unparalleled in Europe.

digSites.name: Bohemian Garnet Museum & Shops
digSites.summary: The historic center for Bohemian pyrope garnet — deep blood-red gems mined in the Czech hills. Several shops and a museum in Prague's old town.
digSites.tips: Bohemian garnets are famous for their deep red color — they've been mined in the Czech Republic since the Middle Ages. Look for certified authentic Bohemian garnet jewelry.

digSites.name: Kimberley Big Hole & Diamond Museum
digSites.summary: The site of the original South African diamond rush. The Big Hole is the world's largest hand-dug excavation. Museum and gift shop on site.
digSites.feeInfo: Museum entry R120 adults. Shop free to browse.
digSites.tips: The Big Hole is a stunning piece of mining history — 214 million tons of rock dug by hand. The museum has excellent diamond displays and replicas of famous stones.

digSites.name: Minas Gerais Crystal Shops & Mines
digSites.summary: The gem and crystal heart of Brazil. Minas Gerais produces tourmaline, aquamarine, topaz, quartz, and the legendary imperial topaz. Numerous shops in the historic colonial town.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse. Prices vary widely.
digSites.tips: Minas Gerais is one of the most gem-rich regions on Earth. Look for imperial topaz — found only here — in golden-orange and pink shades.

digSites.name: Rio Grande do Sul Amethyst Mines
digSites.region: Ametista do Sul, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
digSites.summary: Brazil's amethyst capital. Underground mines in the basalt cliffs produce enormous geode clusters. Several mines offer tours and collecting.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine tours R20–50. Specimens and geodes for sale.
digSites.tips: The amethyst geodes here can weigh hundreds of pounds. The underground mines are cool and damp — bring a jacket. Geodes are priced by weight and quality.

digSites.name: Jaipur Gem Market
digSites.summary: One of the world's great gem cutting and trading centers. Jaipur's Johari Bazaar offers emerald, ruby, sapphire, tanzanite, and countless semi-precious stones.
digSites.tips: Jaipur has been a gem-cutting center for centuries. Visit the Gem Palace for museum-quality pieces. Always ask for certification on expensive gems.

digSites.name: Itoigawa Jade Gorge
digSites.summary: Japan's jade valley — the Itoigawa-Shizuoka Tectonic Line produces some of the world's finest nephrite jade. Museum and limited collecting.
digSites.feeInfo: Museum ¥500. Collecting limited to designated areas.
digSites.tips: Itoigawa is one of the few places in the world where jade is found in its original geological source. The Fossa Magna Museum has excellent jade displays.

digSites.name: Arahura River Pounamu (Greenstone) Area
digSites.summary: The traditional source of pounamu (New Zealand greenstone/jade). The Arahura River is sacred to Māori and produces nephrite and bowenite.
digSites.feeInfo: Free — public river access. Cultural restrictions apply.
digSites.tips: Pounamu is culturally significant to Māori — only Ngāi Tahu can legally extract it, but casual beach finds may be kept. Visit Hokitika's greenstone shops for authentic carvings.

digSites.name: Naica Crystal Cave Visitor Center
digSites.summary: Home of the Giant Crystal Cave — the largest natural crystals ever found (selenite gypsum up to 36 feet long). The cave itself is closed, but a visitor center and mineral shops serve the area.
digSites.feeInfo: Visitor center free. Cave access restricted to scientists.
digSites.tips: The Giant Crystal Cave is inaccessible (50°C with 90% humidity), but the Naica mine area has excellent mineral shops. Mexican selenite and gypsum specimens are world-class.

digSites.name: Las Chispas Silver Mine Shop
digSites.summary: Historic Mexican silver mining region with mineral shops featuring native silver, acanthite, proustite, and pyrargyrite specimens from the famous silver belt.
digSites.tips: Sonora's silver mines have produced some of the finest silver mineral specimens in the world. Ask about locally mined proustite — 'ruby silver' — which is deep red and rare.

digSites.name: Eidsvoll Garnet Area
digSites.summary: Norwegian garnet locality in the Oslo Rift — produces large almandine garnet crystals in mica schist. Some collecting on public forest land.
digSites.tips: Look for dark red garnet porphyroblasts in the exposed mica schist along forest roads. Norway also has famous larvikite (blue anorthosite) quarries nearby.

digSites.name: Chanthaburi Gem Market
digSites.summary: One of the world's largest colored gemstone markets. Famous for ruby and sapphire cutting, with dealers from around the globe gathering every weekend.
digSites.tips: Chanthaburi is one of the world's great gem trading hubs. Go on Saturday for the biggest market. Always ask for certification on expensive stones.

digSites.name: Picos de Europa Quartz Area
digSites.summary: The dramatic Picos de Europa mountains yield clear quartz crystals, calcite, and dolomite from Alpine fissure veins in limestone.
digSites.tips: Search the alpine fissures in the limestone for clear quartz and calcite. The terrain is steep — bring proper hiking gear.

digSites.name: Muzo Emerald Mine Visitor Center
digSites.summary: The world's most famous emerald mine. Muzo produces the finest emeralds on Earth. While the mine itself is private, the area has shops selling rough and cut emeralds.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine tours by arrangement. Shops free to browse.
digSites.tips: Colombian emeralds are the world standard for quality. Only buy from reputable, certified dealers. The Muzo and Chivor mines have produced emeralds for over 1,000 years.

digSites.name: Brandberg Crystal Area
digSites.summary: The Brandberg Massif in the Namib Desert produces world-class smoky quartz, amethyst scepters, and prehnite from Alpine-type fissures in granite.
digSites.feeInfo: Permit required from Namibian Ministry of Mines.
digSites.tips: The Brandberg is one of the finest quartz localities in Africa. The scepter amethysts here are legendary. A collecting permit is required — arrange through a tour operator.

digSites.name: Antananarivo Gem Market
digSites.summary: Madagascar's capital is the trading hub for one of the most mineral-rich islands on Earth — tourmaline, aquamarine, sapphire, beryl, and enormous quartz crystals.
digSites.tips: Madagascar produces some of the world's finest tourmaline and aquamarine. Always buy from established dealers with certification for expensive stones.

digSites.name: Peshawar Gem Market
digSites.summary: The trading hub for Pakistani and Afghan gems — aquamarine from Nagar, tourmaline from Nuristan, lapis lazuli from Afghanistan, and topaz from Katlang.
digSites.tips: Peshawar is the gateway to some of the world's most spectacular pegmatite minerals. The aquamarine from Nagar and the lapis from Afghanistan are world-renowned.

digSites.name: Merelani Tanzanite Mining Area
digSites.summary: The only source of tanzanite in the world — a 4-square-mile mining area producing the blue-violet zoisite variety found nowhere else on Earth.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Shop in nearby Arusha.
digSites.hours: Shops in Arusha daily 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM
digSites.tips: Tanzanite is found in only one place on Earth. The mines are private and dangerous — buy from certified dealers in Arusha. Always ask for grading certificates.

digSites.name: Patagonia Agate Fields
digSites.summary: The Patagonian desert is one of the world's great agate and petrified wood localities. Los Altares and Paso de Indias produce stunning agate nodules.
digSites.feeInfo: Free on provincial land. Some areas require permits.
digSites.tips: The Patagonian agates are world-class — look for banded nodules weathering out of the volcanic rocks. Visit the Paleontological Museum in Trelew for context.

digSites.name: Hunan Mineral Market
digSites.summary: China's major mineral trading hub — famous for stibnite, fluorite, calcite, and cinnabar specimens from Hunan's prolific mineral deposits.
digSites.tips: Hunan produces some of the world's finest stibnite crystals and fluorite specimens. The markets in Changsha serve international mineral collectors.

digSites.name: Mibladen Vanadinite & Barite Area
digSites.summary: World-famous for spectacular red vanadinite crystals and large barite plates. Old mine workings offer collecting with local guides.
digSites.feeInfo: Local guides €20–50 per day. Some mine access fees apply.
digSites.tips: Morocco's vanadinite crystals are the finest in the world — blood-red hexagonal prisms on barite matrix. Hire a local guide in Midelt for the best collecting experience.

digSites.name: Erfoud Fossil Market
digSites.summary: The Sahara's fossil capital. Erfoud's shops sell Devonian trilobites, orthoceras, goniatites, and polished fossil marble slabs from the surrounding desert.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse. Fossils priced individually.
digSites.tips: Erfoud is the fossil capital of Morocco. The Devonian beds nearby produce world-class trilobites. Buy from established shops — beware of composite or fake specimens.

digSites.name: Murun Charoite Massif
digSites.summary: The only source of charoite — a stunning purple chatoyant mineral found only in this remote Siberian massif. Extremely remote; specimens available in shops.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Buy from mineral dealers in Moscow/St. Petersburg.
digSites.hours: Shops in major cities: daily 10:00 AM – 7:00 PM
digSites.tips: Charoite is found in only one place on Earth — the Murun Massif in Siberia. The swirling purple patterns make it one of the most distinctive ornamental stones.

digSites.name: Tin Fields Topaz Area
digSites.summary: Historic tin mining area where alluvial topaz, cassiterite, and quartz crystals can be found in creek gravels. Public fossicking with a permit.
digSites.tips: Pan the creek gravels for topaz crystals — they're colorless to pale blue and can be confused with quartz. A fossicking license is required.

digSites.name: Kings Canyon Opalized Fossils
digSites.summary: The Red Centre has opalized fossils and seams in the sandstone. Limited public fossicking in designated areas of the national park surrounds.
digSites.feeInfo: Free — park surrounds (not inside national park).
digSites.tips: The Red Centre's sandstone holds opal in seams and as opalized fossils. Bring plenty of water — this is remote desert. Check with the ranger station for designated fossicking zones.

digSites.name: Mount Hay Thunderegg Area
digSites.summary: Famous thunderegg (geode) locality in volcanic rhyolite. The Mount Hay area produces spectacular geodes with agate, quartz, and amethyst centers.
digSites.feeInfo: Free fossicking area. Fossicking permit $5 AUD.
digSites.tips: Break open the rhyolite nodules to find agate-filled thundereggs. A small sledgehammer and chisel are essential. The geodes here are among Australia's finest.

digSites.name: Mont Saint-Hilaire
digSites.summary: One of the world's most mineralogically diverse localities — over 400 mineral species, including many found nowhere else. Active quarry with restricted collecting access.
digSites.feeInfo: Collecting by permission only — contact quarry management or mineral clubs.
digSites.tips: Mont Saint-Hilaire is a mineralogist's paradise — over 400 species, many type-locality minerals. Access is restricted; join the Canadian Mineralogical Association or contact quarry management for guided collecting trips.

digSites.name: Jeffrey Mine Quartz Area
digSites.summary: Historic asbestos mine famous for enormous transparent quartz crystals and pink spodumene (kunzite). Mineral collecting on old mine dumps.
digSites.feeInfo: Collecting on dumps — by arrangement with local clubs.
digSites.tips: The Jeffrey Mine produced some of the world's largest quartz crystals — over 1 meter long. The old mine dumps still yield transparent quartz and occasional pink spodumene.

digSites.name: Vancouver Island Quartz & Calcite Area
digSites.summary: Vancouver Island's metamorphic terrain yields clear quartz, calcite, and garnet in veins and stream gravels. Public collecting on Crown land.
digSites.tips: Search the Cowichan River gravels and road cuts for quartz and calcite crystals. Vancouver Island's geology is diverse — from volcanic to metamorphic.

digSites.name: Cornwall Tin & Mineral Area
digSites.summary: The historic heart of Cornish mining — tin, copper, and rare minerals from the world's most famous tin district. Old mine dumps yield cassiterite, chalcopyrite, and more.
digSites.feeInfo: Free — old mine dumps. Museum entry £15.
digSites.hours: Daylight hours. Museum daily 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM.
digSites.tips: Cornwall's mining heritage is UNESCO-recognized. Geevor Tin Mine offers underground tours and mineral collecting on the old dumps. Look for black cassiterite crystals in the granite.

digSites.name: Snowdonia Quartz & Slate Area
digSites.summary: Welsh slate quarries and mountain veins producing quartz, chlorite, and occasional pyrite crystals. Historic slate mining district with spectacular geology.
digSites.feeInfo: Free — some old quarry dumps. National Slate Museum free.
digSites.hours: Daylight hours. Museum daily 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM.
digSites.tips: The Dinorwic slate quarries are enormous and spectacular. Search the waste tips for quartz veins in the slate. The National Slate Museum tells the story of Welsh slate mining.

digSites.name: Scottish Agate Beaches
digSites.summary: The east coast of Scotland is famous for beautiful agates weathered from volcanic rocks. Montrose Beach and Arbroath cliffs yield blue, orange, and banded agates.
digSites.hours: Daylight hours — best at low tide
digSites.tips: Walk the beach at low tide after storms. Scottish agates are found in Old Red Sandstone volcanic rocks — look for waxy, banded pebbles among the beach cobbles.

digSites.name: Saxony Agate & Mineral Area
digSites.summary: German countryside with agate, quartz, and amethyst in volcanic rocks of the Thuringian Forest. Old mine dumps and forest paths yield specimens.
digSites.tips: Search the Thuringian Forest trails for agate in the volcanic rock outcrops. German agates are known for fine banding and rich colors.

digSites.name: Swiss Alps Crystal Area
digSites.summary: Alpine fissure veins in the Swiss Alps produce world-class smoky quartz, clear rock crystal, and pink fluorite. Famous among collectors for 'Gwindel' quartz crystals.
digSites.feeInfo: Collecting permits required from local communes.
digSites.tips: Alpine cleft minerals are found in fissures in granite gneiss. The Swiss produce the world's finest smoky quartz and 'Gwindel' twisted quartz crystals. Get a permit from the local commune office.

digSites.name: Baltic Amber Coast
digSites.summary: The Baltic coast is the world's richest source of amber — 40-million-year-old fossil tree resin. After storms, amber washes up on the beaches of Poland, Lithuania, and Russia.
digSites.tips: Go to the beach after a storm with onshore winds. Amber floats in saltwater and washes up with seaweed. Look for yellow-orange pieces that glow under UV light. The Gdańsk Amber Museum is excellent.

digSites.name: Carrara Marble Quarries
digSites.summary: The world's most famous marble quarries — Michelangelo's source. The white Carrara Marble is a metamorphic limestone prized for over 2,000 years.
digSites.tips: The Carrara quarries have produced marble for the Pantheon, Michelangelo's David, and countless masterpieces. The Marble Museum and quarry tours show active extraction. Spectacular mountain scenery.

digSites.name: Bolivia Amethyst & Quartz Mines
digSites.summary: Bolivian Andes produce amethyst, citrine, and spectacular quartz crystals from hydrothermal veins. Mining cooperative shops sell specimens.
digSites.feeInfo: Free to browse shops. Mine access by arrangement.
digSites.tips: Bolivia produces distinctive amethyst and citrine from Andean veins. The Sapecho area is known for large quartz crystals. Buy from reputable dealers in La Paz.

digSites.name: Chile Copper Mineral Area
digSites.summary: The Atacama Desert is the world's richest copper mining district. Old mine workings yield atacamite, chrysocolla, malachite, and native copper specimens.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Mineral shops in Copiapó.
digSites.tips: The Atacama is the copper capital of the world. Atacamite — a green copper chloride — was named after this desert. Buy specimens from mineral shops in Copiapó or Santiago.

digSites.name: Pasto Bueno Quartz & Wolfram Area
digSites.summary: Peruvian Andes mine producing world-class quartz, hubnerite, and rhodochrosite from hydrothermal veins. High-altitude collecting.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access by arrangement. Shops in Lima.
digSites.tips: Pasto Bueno produces some of the world's finest quartz and hubnerite combinations. The Peruvian Andes are mineral-rich. Buy from mineral dealers in Lima's Gamarra district.

digSites.name: Erongo Mountains Mineral Area
digSites.summary: The Erongo Mountains are Namibia's mineral treasure house — aquamarine, schorl tourmaline, topaz, and quartz from granite pegmatites. Public collecting with permits.
digSites.tips: The Erongo granitic pegmatites produce world-class aquamarine and black tourmaline. Hire a guide in Usakos or Karibib. The area is remote and rugged — bring water and a 4WD vehicle.
