digSites.name: Nigeria Tourmaline Mining Area
digSites.summary: Nigerian pegmatites produce fine tourmaline — green, pink, and watermelon varieties. One of Africa's most important gem sources.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access by arrangement. Shops in Lagos.
digSites.tips: Nigeria is a major tourmaline source — especially green and watermelon varieties. Buy from established dealers in Lagos. Always ask for certification on expensive stones.

digSites.name: Kenya Tsavorite Garnet Area
digSites.summary: The Tsavo region produces tsavorite garnet — a vivid green garnet found only in Kenya and Tanzania. Small-scale mining operations.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Buy in Nairobi.
digSites.tips: Tsavorite is one of the rarest and most beautiful garnets — vivid green from chromium and vanadium. Buy from certified dealers in Nairobi. Named after Tsavo National Park.

digSites.name: South Africa Amethyst & Quartz Area
digSites.summary: South African amethyst mines produce deep purple crystals and geodes. Several small operations welcome visitors and sell specimens.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine tours R50–100. Specimens for sale.
digSites.tips: South African amethyst is known for deep purple color. The Boekenhouthoek area has several small mines. Buy geodes and crystals directly from the miners for the best prices.

digSites.name: Vietnam Ruby & Sapphire Mines
digSites.summary: Vietnam's Luc Yen district produces fine rubies and sapphires from marble-hosted deposits. The area is also known for spinel and tourmaline.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access by arrangement. Markets daily.
digSites.hours: Luc Yen gem market: daily 6:00 AM – 12:00 PM
digSites.tips: Luc Yen has a famous early-morning gem market where miners sell rough rubies and sapphires. Vietnamese rubies are known for their bright, fluorescent red color.

digSites.name: Ratnapura Gem Market
digSites.summary: Sri Lanka's 'City of Gems' has been a sapphire and ruby trading center for over 2,000 years. The Ratnapura gem market is one of the world's great gem destinations.
digSites.tips: Ratnapura means 'City of Gems' in Sinhala. Sri Lanka (Ceylon) is famous for blue sapphires, padparadscha, cat's eye chrysoberyl, and alexandrite. Always ask for certification.

digSites.name: Mogok Ruby Valley
digSites.summary: The legendary Mogok Valley produces the world's finest rubies — the 'pigeon's blood' red stones prized for over 800 years. Also sapphire, spinel, and peridot.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Buy in Yangon.
digSites.hours: Shops in Yangon daily 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM
digSites.tips: Mogok rubies are the world standard for ruby quality. The 'pigeon's blood' color is legendary. Access to Mogok is restricted — buy from reputable dealers in Yangon with certification.

digSites.name: Badakhshan Lapis Lazuli Mines
digSites.summary: The world's oldest and finest source of lapis lazuli — mined for over 6,000 years. The Sar-e-Sang mines produce the deepest blue lapis with pyrite inclusions.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Buy in Kabul.
digSites.hours: Shops in Kabul daily 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM
digSites.tips: Afghan lapis is the world's finest — the source for ancient Egyptian, Mesopotamian, and Renaissance art. The deep blue color with gold pyrite flecks is unmistakable. Buy from established dealers.

digSites.name: Neyshabur Turquoise Mine
digSites.summary: One of the world's oldest and most famous turquoise mines — operated for over 2,000 years. Persian turquoise is prized for its pure blue color.
digSites.tips: Persian turquoise has been mined here since ancient times. The Neyshabur mines produce some of the world's finest turquoise — prized for its uniform blue color without matrix.

digSites.name: Connemara Marble Quarries
digSites.summary: Ireland's famous green marble — a serpentine-rich limestone quarried in Connemara for centuries. Distinctive deep green color with white veining.
digSites.feeInfo: Quarry tours €12. Shop free to browse.
digSites.tips: Connemara Marble is Ireland's national stone — a deep green serpentine marble over 600 million years old. The quarries in the Twelve Bens mountains are iconic. Shop sells polished specimens.

digSites.name: Panasqueira Tungsten Mine
digSites.summary: World-famous for spectacular apatite, ferberite, arsenopyrite, and quartz specimens. The Panasqueira mine is one of Europe's most mineralogically important localities.
digSites.feeInfo: Mine access restricted. Specimens from mineral dealers.
digSites.hours: Shops in Covilhã daily 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM
digSites.tips: Panasqueira produces some of the world's finest apatite crystals — green, blue, and purple. The mine is active and access is restricted. Buy specimens from dealers in Covilhã or at mineral shows.

digSites.name: Greenland Tugtupite Area
digSites.summary: The type locality for tugtupite — a rare fluorescent mineral that glows bright red under UV light. The Ilimaussaq complex is one of Earth's most unusual mineral localities.
digSites.tips: Greenland's Ilimaussaq complex has over 200 rare minerals. Tugtupite fluoresces bright crimson under UV. Only accessible in summer. Arrange tours through Nuuk-based operators.

digSites.name: Querétaro Fire Opal Mines
digSites.summary: Mexico is the world's premier source of fire opal — translucent orange to red opal from volcanic deposits. Several mines offer tours and specimen sales.
digSites.tips: Mexican fire opal comes in orange, cherry red, and yellow. The best stones show play-of-color within the orange body. Buy directly from the mines for the best selection and prices.

blmDigSites.name: Black Hills Rockhound Area
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Fire agate — a brown agate with internal play of red, green, and gold fire
blmDigSites.directions: On the north side of AZ Route 191, ~18 miles north of Safford, just east of milepost 141.
blmDigSites.facilities: No facilities. Dispersed camping allowed up to 14 days. No fees or permits required.

blmDigSites.name: Round Mountain Rockhound Area
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Rocks and mineral specimens — various collectible minerals
blmDigSites.directions: From Highway 70 east of Safford, travel ~50 miles into New Mexico to just beyond milepost 5. Turn right onto the dirt access road and follow signs ~12 miles.
blmDigSites.facilities: No facilities. Remote desert location — bring everything you need.

blmDigSites.name: Chambless Rock Collecting Area
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Hematite, magnetite, green epidote, limestone, marble, tiny dark-red garnets, fossils in gray limestone
blmDigSites.directions: From Needles, take I-40 west ~25 miles to Mountain Springs Rd exit. Go south on National Trails Highway west ~35 miles to BLM Route NS328 (just west of Chambless). Turn right and drive ~2 miles.
blmDigSites.facilities: No facilities. Hiking, horseback riding, and wildlife viewing in the area.

blmDigSites.name: Savahia Peak Rock Collecting Area
blmDigSites.directions: From Needles, take US-95 south ~35 miles to BLM Route NS660 (Pyramid Peak Rd). Turn left and drive ~2 miles. Collecting area is on both sides of the route. Alternative: large wash north of US-62, 2 miles east of Vidal Junction.

blmDigSites.name: Wiley Well Geode Beds
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Geodes with quartz, amethyst, and citrine crystals; nodules
blmDigSites.directions: South of Blythe via Wiley's Well Road. Accessible via BLM Route NS-773. The collecting area includes Hauser Geode Beds and Potato Patch.
blmDigSites.facilities: Wiley's Well Campground nearby with tables, fire rings, pit toilets. Dispersed camping allowed.
blmDigSites.feeInfo: Free collecting; campground has minimal fees

blmDigSites.name: Garnet Hill
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Ruby-red almandine garnets in rhyolite rock
blmDigSites.directions: From Ely, travel west on US-50. 1 mile north of the Ruth turnoff, turn right onto the graded access road. Drive 3.1 miles to the parking area.
blmDigSites.facilities: Four picnic sites with grills, accessible restroom, group BBQ area, two informal tent/camper areas. No water. Elevation 7,000 ft.

blmDigSites.name: Oregon Sunstone Public Collection Area
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Oregon sunstone — a translucent feldspar gemstone in shades of clear, yellow, red, green, and schiller (copper inclusion) varieties
blmDigSites.directions: In the Rabbit Basin, south-central Oregon high desert. From Plush, follow signs via Hogback Road and BLM Roads 6155/6115/6195 to the entrance.
blmDigSites.facilities: Pit toilet, picnic tables, shade structure. Camping allowed anywhere within the collection area.

blmDigSites.name: Glass Buttes Obsidian Area
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Obsidian — black, mahogany, fire, rainbow, and snowflake varieties
blmDigSites.directions: In the Prineville District, off Highway 20 between Bend and Burns. Look for BLM signs marking the Glass Buttes area.
blmDigSites.facilities: No facilities. Dispersed camping permitted on BLM land.

blmDigSites.name: Topaz Mountain Rockhound Recreation Area
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Topaz crystals — Utah's state gemstone, plus other minerals like bixbyite, pseudobrookite, and garnet
blmDigSites.directions: 55 miles west of Delta via US Highway 6 and paved county road. In the Fillmore Field Office area.

blmDigSites.name: Dugway Geode Beds
blmDigSites.whatToFind: Geodes — often quartz varieties including clear quartz, amethyst, and rose quartz
blmDigSites.directions: From Salt Lake City: I-80 west to exit 99 (SH-36). After ~33 miles, turn right onto the old Pony Express Rd at Faust. ~50 miles along Pony Express Trail/Simpson Springs Rd to a signed turnoff, then ~2 miles on unimproved road.
blmDigSites.facilities: No on-site facilities. Contact Fillmore Field Office for info. Dispersed camping allowed.

trailheads.name: Black Hills Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access point for the Black Hills Rockhound Area — fire agate collecting. Trailhead leads to the designated BLM digging zone.

trailheads.name: Chambless Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to hematite, magnetite, epidote, and garnet collecting area along BLM Route NS328.

trailheads.name: Wiley Well Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to geode beds including Hauser Geode Beds and Potato Patch. Near Wiley's Well Campground.

trailheads.name: Savahia Peak Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to bright white chalcedony collecting area along BLM Route NS660.

trailheads.name: Mount Antero Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to high-altitude aquamarine and phenakite collecting on Mount Antero. Trailhead at Clear Creek Reservoir — 4WD road to 13,000 ft. Best July through September.

trailheads.name: Crystal Peak Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to amazonite, smoky quartz, and topaz collecting in the Pikes Peak granite. Popular BLM/Forest Service area near Florissant Fossil Beds.

trailheads.name: Emerald Creek Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to star garnet collecting area in the Emerald Creek drainage. One of only two places in the world where star garnets are found. Permit required from Potlatch (Panhandle) BLM.

trailheads.name: Mores Creek Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to smoky quartz and aquamarine collecting in the Boise Basin area. BLM land along Mores Creek.

trailheads.name: Rock Creek Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to sapphire gravels along Rock Creek. BLM and USFS land — sapphire screening is popular. Look for the Gem Mountain sapphire area nearby.

trailheads.name: Missouri River Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to agate and sapphire gravels along the Missouri River. BLM land near Canyon Ferry and Hauser Lake.

trailheads.name: Garnet Hill Trailhead
trailheads.description: Trailhead at 7,000 ft elevation with picnic sites. Access to garnet collecting on rhyolite ridge. Four picnic sites with grills and accessible restroom.

trailheads.name: Rockhound State Park Area Trailhead
trailheads.description: While Rockhound State Park is state-managed, surrounding BLM land offers thunderegg and geode collecting. Access via BLM roads south of Deming.

trailheads.name: Sunstone Area Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to the Oregon Sunstone Public Collection Area in the Rabbit Basin. Pit toilet, picnic tables, and shade structure available.

trailheads.name: Glass Buttes Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to the Glass Buttes obsidian collecting area off Highway 20. Multiple obsidian varieties available at the surface.

trailheads.name: Black Hills Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to rose quartz and mica collecting areas in the Black Hills. BLM and Forest Service land near Custer. Look for the famous Fairburn agate gravels.

trailheads.name: Topaz Mountain Trailhead
trailheads.description: 55 miles west of Delta. Trailhead provides access to topaz collecting area in the Thomas Range. Dispersed camping permitted.

trailheads.name: Dugway Geode Beds Trailhead
trailheads.description: Remote trailhead via the Pony Express Trail. Access to geode collecting beds. Requires high-clearance vehicle for unimproved roads.

trailheads.name: Saddle Mountain Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to petrified wood and agate collecting on BLM land near Saddle Mountain. Popular spring and fall collecting.

trailheads.name: Jade Mountain Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to nephrite jade collecting areas in the Granite Mountains. BLM land along the Sweetwater River. Look for dark green to black jade boulders.

trailheads.name: Sweetwater River Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to jade and agate gravels along the Sweetwater River. BLM land — look for jade in alluvial deposits.

trailheads.name: Jade Mountain Trailhead
trailheads.description: Remote access to nephrite jade deposits in the Jade Mountains. Extremely remote — access by bush plane or boat. Not for casual collectors.

trailheads.name: Resurrection Creek Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to recreational gold panning on BLM land along Resurrection Creek. Popular day-use area on the Kenai Peninsula.

trailheads.name: Walls of Jericho Trailhead
trailheads.description: Popular hiking trail through Jackson County canyon with creek-bed rock and mineral collecting. Managed by Alabama State Lands, not BLM. Quartz, chert, and sandstone formations.

trailheads.name: Crater of Diamonds Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to the only public diamond mine in the world. State park fee-dig — keep what you find. Also find amethyst, garnet, jasper, and agate.

trailheads.name: Wegner Quartz Crystal Mines Trailhead
trailheads.description: Popular fee-dig quartz crystal collecting in the Ouachita Mountains. Private operation — access by appointment. World-class clear and smoky quartz.

trailheads.name: Afton Canyon Trailhead
trailheads.description: BLM-managed canyon along the Mojave River. Access to travertine, calcite, and various minerals. Known as the 'Grand Canyon of the Mojave.' Popular year-round.

trailheads.name: Strickland Quarry Access
trailheads.description: Historic mineral collecting site famous for tourmaline, beryl, and garnet. Private quarry — access by permission or organized mineral club field trips only.

trailheads.name: Cape Henlopen Trailhead
trailheads.description: Beach collecting for fossils and quartz pebbles along the Atlantic shore. State park, not BLM. Look for fossilized shell fragments in the sand.

trailheads.name: Peace River Trailhead
trailheads.description: Popular fossil hunting area — megalodon teeth, ray plates, and mammal bones. Private and state lands — access via canoe outfitters. Florida fossil permit required.

trailheads.name: Graves Mountain Access
trailheads.description: Famous mineral locality — rutile, lazulite, pyrophyllite, and kyanite. Annual mineral society digs open to the public. Managed by Georgia DNR.

trailheads.name: Papakolea Green Sand Beach Trailhead
trailheads.description: Hiking access to one of the world's only green sand beaches — olivine-rich sands. Collecting sand is prohibited; viewing only. Managed by Hawaii County.

trailheads.name: Keokuk Geode Beds Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to the famous Keokuk geode beds along the Des Moines River. Private quarries offer fee-dig access — geodes filled with quartz, chalcedony, and calcite.

trailheads.name: Cave-in-Rock Fluorite District Trailhead
trailheads.description: Historic fluorite mining district. Private fee-dig mines offer fluorite, calcite, barite, and galena. Southern Illinois was once the largest fluorite producer in the U.S.

trailheads.name: Falls of the Ohio Trailhead
trailheads.description: Exposed Devonian fossil beds on the Ohio River — corals, brachiopods, and crinoids. State park interpretive center; collecting is restricted to certain areas.

trailheads.name: Monument Rocks Trailhead
trailheads.description: Niobrara Chalk formations with marine fossils — shark teeth, fish vertebrae, and invertebrates. BLM land and private land mixed — verify boundaries. Smoky Hill Chalk badlands.

trailheads.name: Clement Mineral District Trailhead
trailheads.description: Historic fluorspar district in western Kentucky. Private fee-dig mines offer fluorite, calcite, and sphalerite specimens. Visit the Ben E. Clement Mineral Museum for guidance.

trailheads.name: Vernon Parish Opal Area Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to Louisiana opal (quartz-opalite) collecting area in the Kisatchie National Forest. USFS-managed, not BLM. Also petrified palm wood — the state fossil.

trailheads.name: Mount Mica Access
trailheads.description: Historic tourmaline and beryl locality — the first gem tourmaline discovered in North America. Private mine — fee-dig by appointment. Western Maine pegmatite belt.

trailheads.name: Newry Mineral Area Trailhead
trailheads.description: World-famous pegmatite minerals — tourmaline, beryl, apatite, and lepidolite. Private quarries with fee-dig access. Annual Maine Mineral & Gem Show nearby.

trailheads.name: Soldier's Delight Trailhead
trailheads.description: Serpentinite barrens with chromite and serpentine minerals. Maryland Environmental Trust area — collecting limited to surface finds. Historic chromite mining district.

trailheads.name: Chester Emery Mines Access
trailheads.description: Historic emery mine district — emery, corundum, and diaspore. Private land and state forest — access via mineral club field trips. Hampden County.

trailheads.name: Keweenaw Peninsula Trailhead
trailheads.description: World-famous native copper collecting area. Old mine dumps and road cuts yield copper, calcite, and prehnite. State and private land mixed — verify access.

trailheads.name: North Shore Agate Trailhead
trailheads.description: Beach collecting for Lake Superior agates along the North Shore. State parks and road cuts — the Lake Superior agate is the Minnesota state gemstone.

trailheads.name: Mississippi Petrified Forest Trailhead
trailheads.description: Petrified wood collecting area. Private park with petrified logs on display; surrounding state and private lands may yield specimens. State fossil is the prehistoric whale Zygorhiza.

trailheads.name: Viburnum Trend Access
trailheads.description: Active mining district famous for galena, calcite, chalcopyrite, and marcasite specimens. Private mine dumps — access via mineral clubs or fee-dig events.

trailheads.name: Blue River Agate Trailhead
trailheads.description: Creek-bed collecting for Blue River agates and Sioux quartzite cobbles. State and county land — verify access. Nebraska is also known for Prairie Agate.

trailheads.name: Franklin Mineral Museum Access
trailheads.description: World capital of fluorescent minerals — willemite, calcite, franklinite. Fee-dig on the old mine dumps behind the museum. Over 350 mineral species found here.

trailheads.name: Herkimer Diamond Trailhead
trailheads.description: Access to Herkimer diamond (doubly-terminated quartz) collecting. Private fee-dig mines — Ace of Diamonds and Herkimer Diamond Mines. Also garnet nearby in the Adirondacks.

trailheads.name: Emerald Hollow Mine Trailhead
trailheads.description: Fee-dig emerald, sapphire, ruby, and aquamarine collecting. The only emerald mine in the U.S. open to the public. Private operation in Alexander County.

trailheads.name: Little Missouri River Trailhead
trailheads.description: Badlands area with petrified wood and lignite. Theodore Roosevelt National Park area — collecting restricted inside park boundaries; check surrounding BLM and state lands.

trailheads.name: Flint Ridge Trailhead
trailheads.description: Historic flint collecting area — Ohio's state gemstone. State memorial with surface collecting permitted. Native American toolstone source for thousands of years.

trailheads.name: Great Salt Plains Trailhead
trailheads.description: Selenite crystal digging area — hourglass-shaped crystals unique to this location. State park dig area open April through October. Also barite rose rocks nearby.

trailheads.name: Deer Hill Access
trailheads.description: Quartz, pyrite, and copper minerals in the Lehigh Valley area. Private quarries — access via mineral clubs. Also historic Cornwall iron mine area.

trailheads.name: Conimicut Point Trailhead
trailheads.description: Beach collecting for quartz pebbles and occasional glacial erratics. State shore access — no BLM land in Rhode Island. Limited mineral collecting in the state.

trailheads.name: Diamond Hill Mine Trailhead
trailheads.description: Fee-dig quartz crystal, amethyst, and smoky quartz collecting. Private mine open to the public. South Carolina's best-known rockhounding destination.

trailheads.name: Elmwood Mine Access
trailheads.description: World-class fluorite, calcite, sphalerite, and barite specimens. Private mine — access via mineral dealers and organized field trips. Central Tennessee zinc mining district.

trailheads.name: Mason County Topaz Trailhead
trailheads.description: Topaz collecting in Mason County — the Texas state gem. Private ranches offer fee-dig access. Also agate, petrified wood, and smoky quartz in the Hill Country.

trailheads.name: Morefield Mine Trailhead
trailheads.description: Fee-dig amazonite, topaz, mica, and garnet collecting. Private mine open seasonally. One of the best pegmatite collecting sites on the East Coast.

trailheads.name: Eden Asbestos Quarry Access
trailheads.description: Grossular garnet, diopside, and vesuvianite in the historic asbestos quarry area. Private and state land — access via mineral clubs. Vermont state mineral is grossular garnet.

trailheads.name: Seneca Rocks Trailhead
trailheads.description: Quartzite formations in the Potomac Highlands. USFS-managed (Monongahela National Forest). Surrounding creeks yield fossils and quartzite specimens.

trailheads.name: Keweenaw Point Trailhead
trailheads.description: Lake Superior agate and copper mineral collecting along the south shore. State and county land — also lead/zinc minerals in the southwest Wisconsin driftless area.

campgrounds.name: Black Hills Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping allowed up to 14 days at the Black Hills Rockhound Area. No facilities — bring everything you need. Best October through April.

campgrounds.name: Wiley's Well Campground
campgrounds.description: Closest campground to the Wiley Well Geode Beds. Tables, fire rings, and pit toilets. Good base for geode collecting trips.

campgrounds.name: Midland Campground
campgrounds.description: BLM dispersed camping area in the Mojave Desert. No facilities. Good base for exploring surrounding BLM rockhounding areas.

campgrounds.name: Clear Creek Campground
campgrounds.description: BLM campground near Mount Antero collecting areas. Basic sites with pit toilets. Popular base camp for summer collecting trips.

campgrounds.name: Fourmile Travel Management Area Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping on BLM land in the Fourmile area. Access to multiple collecting sites in the Arkansas River Valley.

campgrounds.name: Emerald Creek Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping near the star garnet collecting area. No facilities. Beautiful forested setting in the Idaho panhandle.

campgrounds.name: Rock Creek Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping along Rock Creek near sapphire collecting areas. No facilities. Creek access for sapphire screening.

campgrounds.name: Garnet Hill Picnic Area
campgrounds.description: Four picnic sites with grills, accessible restroom, and group BBQ area. Two informal tent/camper areas. No water. Elevation 7,000 ft.

campgrounds.name: Sunstone Collection Area Camping
campgrounds.description: Camping is allowed anywhere within the Oregon Sunstone Public Collection Area. Pit toilet, picnic tables, and shade structure on-site.

campgrounds.name: Glass Buttes Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping permitted on BLM land at Glass Buttes. No facilities. Great base for obsidian collecting off Highway 20.

campgrounds.name: Black Hills BLM Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping on BLM land in the Black Hills. Access to rose quartz and agate collecting areas. No facilities.

campgrounds.name: Simpson Springs Campground
campgrounds.description: BLM campground along the Pony Express Trail, near the Dugway Geode Beds. Good base camp for geode collecting expeditions.

campgrounds.name: Topaz Mountain Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping permitted at Topaz Mountain Rockhound Recreation Area. No facilities. Plan for remote desert conditions.

campgrounds.name: Saddle Mountain BLM Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping on BLM land near Saddle Mountain petrified wood area. No facilities. Spring and fall are best.

campgrounds.name: Sweetwater Campground
campgrounds.description: BLM campground along the Sweetwater River. Basic sites. Good base for jade and agate collecting in the Granite Mountains.

campgrounds.name: Resurrection Creek Dispersed Camping
campgrounds.description: Dispersed camping on BLM land along Resurrection Creek. Near recreational gold panning area. No facilities.

campgrounds.name: DeSoto State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: Developed campground near Little River Canyon. Good base for exploring Alabama's Appalachian geology. State park with full facilities — not BLM.

campgrounds.name: Crater of Diamonds State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: Full-service campground adjacent to the diamond search area. State park, not BLM. Good base for quartz crystal collecting in the Ouachita Mountains.

campgrounds.name: Gus's Ozark Mountain Campground
campgrounds.description: Private campground near Wegner Quartz Crystal Mines. Good base for quartz crystal fee-dig operations in the Mount Ida area.

campgrounds.name: Afton Canyon Campground
campgrounds.description: BLM campground in Afton Canyon with pit toilets and fire rings. Mojave River runs seasonally. Good base for desert rockhounding. No water.

campgrounds.name: Rockhound State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground adjacent to BLM land. Water, electric, and restrooms. Collecting allowed in the park — thundereggs, geodes, and jasper.

campgrounds.name: Hammonasset State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near Long Island Sound. Not a rockhounding site but good base for southern Connecticut mineral localities and beach collecting.

campgrounds.name: Cape Henlopen State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground with full facilities near the Atlantic shore. Good base for beach fossil and mineral collecting along the Delaware coast.

campgrounds.name: Peace River Campground & Canoe
campgrounds.description: Private campground on the Peace River — popular base for fossil hunting canoe trips. Megalodon teeth and mammal bones. Florida fossil permit required.

campgrounds.name: Elijah Clark State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near Graves Mountain mineral locality. Full facilities on J. Strom Thurmond Lake. Good base for Georgia mineral collecting.

campgrounds.name: Namahanoa (Green Sand) Campground
campgrounds.description: Rustic camping near South Point — the southernmost point in the U.S. Near Papakolea Green Sand Beach. Hawaii County managed — no facilities. Collecting sand prohibited.

campgrounds.name: Geode State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near the Keokuk geode beds. Good base for geode collecting in southeast Iowa. Full facilities.

campgrounds.name: Ferne Clyffe State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near the Cave-in-Rock fluorite district. Full facilities. Good base for southern Illinois mineral collecting.

campgrounds.name: Charlestown State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near the Falls of the Ohio fossil beds. Full facilities. Good base for fossil collecting along the Ohio River.

campgrounds.name: Wilson State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground on Wilson Lake. Good base for exploring the Smoky Hill Chalk badlands and Monument Rocks area in western Kansas.

campgrounds.name: Lake Barkley State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park resort campground in the western Kentucky fluorspar district. Full facilities. Good base for fluorite and calcite collecting.

campgrounds.name: Kisatchie National Forest Campground
campgrounds.description: USFS campground in the Vernon Parish area — near Louisiana opal collecting sites. Full facilities. Also good for petrified palm wood.

campgrounds.name: Mount Blue State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in the western Maine pegmatite belt. Good base for tourmaline and beryl fee-dig quarries in the Newry-Paris area.

campgrounds.name: Patapsco Valley State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near the Soldier's Delight serpentinite barrens. Full facilities. Good base for central Maryland mineral localities.

campgrounds.name: Chester-Blandford State Forest Campground
campgrounds.description: State forest campground near the historic Chester Emery Mines. Rustic sites. Good base for western Massachusetts mineral collecting.

campgrounds.name: McLain State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground on the Keweenaw Peninsula. Good base for native copper collecting at old mine dumps. Lake Superior shoreline.

campgrounds.name: Tettegouche State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground on the North Shore. Excellent base for Lake Superior agate beach collecting. Full facilities along Lake Superior.

campgrounds.name: Leroy Percy State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in the Mississippi Delta. Good base for petrified wood and fossil collecting in west-central Mississippi.

campgrounds.name: Onondaga Cave State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near the Viburnum mining district. Full facilities. Good base for galena, calcite, and chalcopyrite collecting.

campgrounds.name: Smith Falls State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near the Niobrara River. Good base for prairie agate and fossil collecting in north-central Nebraska.

campgrounds.name: High Point State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in northern New Jersey. Good base for Franklin and Sterling Hill fluorescent mineral collecting sites.

campgrounds.name: Herkimer Diamond Mines KOA
campgrounds.description: Private campground adjacent to Herkimer Diamond Mines fee-dig area. Full RV and tent sites. Direct access to quartz crystal collecting.

campgrounds.name: Emerald Hollow Mine Camping
campgrounds.description: Private campground at the Emerald Hollow Mine fee-dig site. Tent and RV sites. Direct access to emerald, sapphire, and ruby collecting.

campgrounds.name: Sully Creek State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near Theodore Roosevelt National Park. Good base for petrified wood and badlands geology in western North Dakota.

campgrounds.name: Dillon State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near Flint Ridge. Full facilities. Good base for flint and Ordovician fossil collecting in central Ohio.

campgrounds.name: Great Salt Plains State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground adjacent to the selenite crystal dig area. Full facilities. Good base for barite rose rock collecting in central Oklahoma.

campgrounds.name: Ricketts Glen State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in northeastern Pennsylvania. Good base for mineral collecting in the Lehigh Valley and Cornwall iron district.

campgrounds.name: Burlingame State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in southern Rhode Island. Good base for beach collecting along the Rhode Island shore. Full facilities.

campgrounds.name: Hickory Knob State Resort Campground
campgrounds.description: State resort campground near the Diamond Hill Mine fee-dig area. Full facilities on Lake Thurmond. Good base for South Carolina mineral collecting.

campgrounds.name: Montgomery Bell State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in central Tennessee. Good base for fluorite and calcite collecting in the Elmwood-Carthage mining district.

campgrounds.name: Inks Lake State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in the Texas Hill Country. Good base for topaz collecting in Mason County and agate hunting in the Llano uplift area.

campgrounds.name: Pocahontas State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground near Richmond. Good base for Morefield Mine fee-dig trips in Amelia and unakite collecting in the Blue Ridge.

campgrounds.name: Little River State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground in northern Vermont. Good base for garnet collecting in the Eden asbestos quarry area and Green Mountain mineral localities.

campgrounds.name: Seneca Shadows Campground
campgrounds.description: USFS campground near Seneca Rocks in the Monongahela National Forest. Good base for quartzite and fossil collecting in the Potomac Highlands.

campgrounds.name: Wyalusing State Park Campground
campgrounds.description: State park campground at the confluence of the Wisconsin and Mississippi Rivers. Good base for lead/zinc minerals and Lake Superior agates in southwest Wisconsin.

stateParks.name: Kartchner Caverns State Park
stateParks.description: A living limestone cave with world-class formations including one of the longest soda straw stalactites in the world. The caverns were discovered in 1974 and preserve spectacular calcite and aragonite formations.

stateParks.name: Lost Dutchman State Park
stateParks.description: Located in the Superstition Mountains, this park features dramatic volcanic rock formations and is steeped in gold mining legend. Hiking trails pass through rhyolite and tuff formations with views of the iconic Flatiron peak.

stateParks.name: Red Rock State Park
stateParks.description: A 286-acre nature preserve showcasing Sedona's iconic red rock formations — sculpted sandstone and shale in vibrant orange and red. The park offers guided geology walks explaining the area's ancient depositional environment.

stateParks.name: Catalina State Park
stateParks.description: Nestled at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains, this park features exposed metamorphic and igneous rock formations, including gneiss and granite. Rich in desert mineral specimens and ancient Hohokam petroglyphs.

stateParks.name: Oracle State Park
stateParks.description: A 4,000-acre park in the Santa Catalina foothills featuring granite outcrops and diverse desert geology. The park's elevation transition zone showcases dramatic changes in rock types and vegetation.

stateParks.name: Lyman Lake State Park
stateParks.description: A reservoir park surrounded by volcanic badlands and petrified wood deposits. Nearby petroglyph sites and the rich volcanic geology make this a unique rockhounding destination.

stateParks.name: Tonto Natural Bridge State Park
stateParks.description: Home to the world's largest natural travertine bridge — 183 feet high and 400 feet long. The bridge formed over thousands of years as mineral-laden springs deposited travertine limestone.

stateParks.name: Homolovi State Park
stateParks.description: An archaeological park featuring ancient Hopi settlements amid sandstone and shale formations. The area contains petrified wood and colorful Chinle Formation deposits.

stateParks.name: Chino Hills State Park
stateParks.description: Rolling hills exposing marine sedimentary rocks and fossils. The park's geology tells the story of ancient sea floors uplifted into the Puente Hills, with visible fossil beds in shale outcrops.

stateParks.name: Mount Tamalpais State Park
stateParks.description: Features Franciscan Complex rocks including chert, serpentinite, and greywacke sandstone — classic examples of California's subduction zone geology. Panoramic views of the Bay Area.

stateParks.name: Malibu Creek State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic volcanic and sedimentary rock formations in the Santa Monica Mountains. The park features visible conglomerate cliffs, volcanic intrusions, and ancient marine fossils.

stateParks.name: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Sonoma Volcanics and Franciscan metamorphic rocks. Hiking trails reveal volcanic ash deposits, obsidian fragments, and ancient river gravels in the Mayacamas Mountains.

stateParks.name: Trione-Annadel State Park
stateParks.description: Known for volcanic rock formations, cobblestone quarries, and rare bentonite clay deposits. The park's geology includes basalt flows, obsidian, and petrified wood.

stateParks.name: Henry W. Coe State Park
stateParks.description: California's second-largest state park features Franciscan chert, serpentinite, and sandstone. The rugged terrain exposes ancient seafloor rocks uplifted during the formation of the Coast Ranges.

stateParks.name: Montaña de Oro State Park
stateParks.description: Spectacular coastal cliffs exposing Miocene marine sedimentary rocks with abundant fossil shells. The park's name ('Mountain of Gold') comes from golden wildflowers covering the volcanic bluffs.

stateParks.name: Cuyamaca Rancho State Park
stateParks.description: Features granitic rocks of the Peninsular Ranges batholith, with quartz veins and mineralized zones. Historic gold mining sites and gem-quality mineral occurrences throughout.

stateParks.name: Golden Gate Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: Exposed Precambrian metamorphic rocks including gneiss and schist, with dramatic pegmatite veins containing quartz and feldspar. Over 28 miles of trails through ancient mountain geology.

stateParks.name: Roxborough State Park
stateParks.description: A National Natural Landmark featuring dramatic tilted red sandstone Fountain Formation rocks — the same formation seen at Red Rocks. Ancient Pennsylvanian-Permian geology with visible angular unconformities.

stateParks.name: Mueller State Park
stateParks.description: Pikes Peak granite dominates this high-elevation park, with visible quartz veins and pegmatite deposits. Excellent examples of weathered granite domes and glacial features.

stateParks.name: Staunton State Park
stateParks.description: Features dramatic granite outcrops of the Pikes Peak batholith, with embedded quartz crystals and feldspar. Historic sawmill and homestead sites amid spectacular rock formations.

stateParks.name: Eldorado Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: World-renowned for its dramatic sandstone cliffs — the Fountain Formation exposed in vertical walls up to 800 feet. The canyon contains visible cross-bedding and ancient stream deposits.

stateParks.name: Lory State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Precambrian metamorphic rocks and sedimentary formations along the Horsetooth Reservoir. Visible pegmatite dikes and migmatite throughout the park's trails.

stateParks.name: Sylvan Lake State Park
stateParks.description: Surrounded by the White River National Forest, featuring sedimentary rock formations and glacial carved valleys. Excellent examples of Leadville limestone and Sawatch quartzite.

stateParks.name: Chatfield State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Denver Formation sedimentary rocks with visible ancient river deposits. The area contains petrified wood specimens and volcanic ash layers from ancient eruptions.

stateParks.name: Silver Falls State Park
stateParks.description: Oregon's largest state park features 10 spectacular waterfalls cutting through Columbia River Basalt flows. The South Falls drops 177 feet over exposed basalt columns — a geological wonder.

stateParks.name: Smith Rock State Park
stateParks.description: World-famous for rock climbing on dramatic welded tuff and basalt columns. The Crooked River carved a canyon through volcanic ash deposits from the John Day Formation.

stateParks.name: Cape Lookout State Park
stateParks.description: Features basaltic headland from Columbia River Basalt Group lava flows, with visible pillow basalts at the base. Miocene-age marine fossils found in sedimentary layers between flows.

stateParks.name: Ecola State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic coastline featuring basalt sea stacks and pillow lavas. Haystack Rock is an iconic volcanic remnant. Ancient sedimentary rocks contain marine fossils.

stateParks.name: Valley Falls State Recreation Area
stateParks.description: Features obsidian deposits and volcanic glass formations from the Modoc Plateau. The area is rich in volcanic minerals and semi-precious stones.

stateParks.name: Sumpter Valley Dredge State Park
stateParks.description: Historic gold dredging site exposing placer deposits and ancient river gravels. The tailings show layers of volcanic tuff and sedimentary deposits from the Blue Mountains.

stateParks.name: The Cove Palisades State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic canyon walls expose layered basalt flows and interbeded sedimentary deposits. The Crooked and Deschutes Rivers carved through volcanic formations creating 700-foot cliffs.

stateParks.name: Otter Crest State Scenic Viewpoint
stateParks.description: Cape Foulweather exposes basaltic rocks from the Columbia River Basalt Group. Stunning ocean views of volcanic headlands with visible columnar jointing.

stateParks.name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
stateParks.description: One of the largest batholiths in the United States — a massive pink granite dome rising 425 feet above the surrounding Hill Country. Exfoliation domes and rock pools showcase Precambrian geology dating back 1 billion years.

stateParks.name: Palo Duro Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: The 'Grand Canyon of Texas' exposes Permian and Triassic sedimentary rocks — dramatic red, orange, and purple sandstone and shale layers carved by the Prairie Dog Town Fork Red River.

stateParks.name: Caprock Canyons State Park
stateParks.description: Features dramatic caprock escarpment geology where the High Plains meet the Rolling Plains. Exposed red Permian sandstone and shale layers with visible unconformities.

stateParks.name: Hueco Tanks State Park & Historic Site
stateParks.description: Unique syenite porphyry rock formations with natural tanks (huecos) that trap rainwater. World-class bouldering and ancient rock art amid dramatic volcanic geology.

stateParks.name: Seminole Canyon State Park & Historic Site
stateParks.description: Limestone canyons with globally significant rock art dating back 4,000+ years. The geology exposes Cretaceous-era Edwards Limestone with fossil-rich layers.

stateParks.name: Colorado Bend State Park
stateParks.description: Features Gorman Cave — a limestone cave with spectacular formations. The park exposes Cretaceous limestone with abundant marine fossils and travertine deposits along springs.

stateParks.name: Independence Park / Pedernales Falls
stateParks.description: Pedernales Falls exposes ancient Cretaceous limestone layers carved by the Pedernales River. Dramatic cascading waterfalls over 300-million-year-old rock formations.

stateParks.name: Lost Maples State Natural Area
stateParks.description: Limestone canyons with dramatic cliffs and spring-fed pools. The Edwards Plateau geology features fossil-rich Cretaceous limestone and unique karst formations.

stateParks.name: Valley of Fire State Park
stateParks.description: Nevada's oldest state park features spectacular Aztec Sandstone formations — 150-million-year-old petrified sand dunes in brilliant red and orange. Ancient petroglyphs and petrified wood throughout.

stateParks.name: Spring Mountain Ranch State Park
stateParks.description: Located in the Red Rock Canyon area, exposing dramatic Keystone Thrust fault where older gray limestone was pushed over younger red sandstone — a classic geological cross-section.

stateParks.name: Cathedral Gorge State Park
stateParks.description: Erooded bentonite clay formations create dramatic cathedral-like spires and slot canyons. The soft volcanic ash deposits are from ancient eruptions of the nearby Caliente caldera.

stateParks.name: Echo Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: Features exposed sedimentary and volcanic rock formations along a scenic reservoir. The area contains mineralized veins and historic mining sites.

stateParks.name: Beaver Dam State Park
stateParks.description: Remote park featuring volcanic rock formations, natural arches, and mineral deposits. The area's geology includes rhyolite and andesite from ancient volcanic activity.

stateParks.name: Kershaw-Ryan State Park
stateParks.description: Nestled in Eagle Canyon with dramatic volcanic rock walls. The park exposes colorful tuff and rhyolite formations with visible mineral staining.

stateParks.name: Big Bend of the Colorado State Recreation Area
stateParks.description: Exposes Colorado River sedimentary deposits and ancient volcanic rocks. The area contains mineralized zones and interesting desert geology along the river.

stateParks.name: Spring Valley State Park
stateParks.description: Features dramatic volcanic tuff formations and historic mining sites. Eagle Valley Reservoir is surrounded by colorful rock outcrops rich in mineral specimens.

stateParks.name: Snow Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: Stunning red and white Navajo Sandstone formations with petrified sand dunes, lava flows, and cinder cones. The park showcases both ancient desert geology and recent volcanic activity.

stateParks.name: Dead Horse Point State Park
stateParks.description: Spectacular overlook of the Colorado River's gooseneck meanders through layered Permian and Pennsylvanian sedimentary rocks. Classic cutaway view of Canyonlands geology.

stateParks.name: Goblin Valley State Park
stateParks.description: Thousands of hoodoos — weathered goblin-shaped rock formations carved from Entrada Sandstone. The soft sandstone creates otherworldly shapes from wind and water erosion.

stateParks.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park
stateParks.description: Vibrant pink-orange sand dunes formed from Navajo Sandstone erosion. The sand grains are tinted by iron oxides — a living example of how sandstone is formed and eroded.

stateParks.name: Antelope Island State Park
stateParks.description: The largest island in the Great Salt Lake features Precambrian metamorphic and igneous rocks — some of the oldest visible rocks in Utah. Fringing mineral deposits along the shoreline.

stateParks.name: Wasatch Mountain State Park
stateParks.description: Features exposed sedimentary and metamorphic rocks of the Wasatch Range. Glacial moraines and ancient river deposits visible along trails. Mineral springs in the area.

stateParks.name: Edge of the Cedars State Park
stateParks.description: Ancient Puebloan site with exposed Morrison Formation rocks — the same formation that yields dinosaur fossils across the Colorado Plateau. Rich in Jurassic-age geology.

stateParks.name: Huntington State Park
stateParks.description: Reservoir park exposing Cretaceous-age sedimentary rocks of the Wasatch Plateau. Coal deposits and fossil-bearing shales visible in nearby road cuts.

stateParks.name: City of Rocks State Park
stateParks.description: Spectacular volcanic rock formations — giant boulders of welded tuff sculpted by erosion into pillars, spires, and balanced rocks. Unique geological formations resembling a city of stone.

stateParks.name: Rockhound State Park
stateParks.description: One of the few state parks specifically designated for rock collecting! Visitors can collect up to 15 pounds of rocks including quartz crystals, geodes, agate, jasper, and perlite.

stateParks.name: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park
stateParks.description: Dog Canyon exposes dramatic sedimentary rock layers of the Sacramento Mountains. The park features visible fossil beds and ancient marine deposits from the Permian period.

stateParks.name: Leasburg Dam State Park
stateParks.description: Exposed volcanic and sedimentary rocks along the Rio Grande. The nearby Soledad Canyon contains interesting volcanic tuff and basalt formations.

stateParks.name: Elephant Butte Lake State Park
stateParks.description: Named for a volcanic core that resembles an elephant. The area exposes volcanic rocks, sedimentary formations, and mineralized zones from ancient hydrothermal activity.

stateParks.name: Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad State Park
stateParks.description: Traverses dramatic volcanic and sedimentary geology of the San Juan Mountains. Exposed rock layers include volcanic tuff, basalt flows, and fossil-bearing sedimentary deposits.

stateParks.name: Hyde Memorial State Park
stateParks.description: Features Precambrian metamorphic and igneous rocks of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. Granite outcrops and pegmatite veins visible along trails.

stateParks.name: Bottomless Lakes State Park
stateParks.description: Unique sinkhole lakes formed in gypsum and red bed sediments. The park exposes Permian-age evaporite deposits and karst geology — a window into ancient sea environments.

stateParks.name: Bannack State Park
stateParks.description: Ghost town park with rich gold mining geology. Placer gold deposits and hard-rock veins in Precambrian metamorphic rocks. Historic mining artifacts amid geological features.

stateParks.name: MacKerricher State Park
stateParks.description: Features dramatic coastal bluffs exposing Franciscan Complex rocks including chert, greywacke, and serpentinite. Tide pools reveal ancient marine geology.

stateParks.name: Wild Horse Island State Park
stateParks.description: Island in Flathead Lake featuring exposed Belt Supergroup sedimentary rocks — ancient Precambrian deposits over 1.4 billion years old. Dramatic sedimentary layering visible.

stateParks.name: Missouri River Headwaters State Park
stateParks.description: Confluence of three rivers forming the Missouri. Exposes Madison Limestone with visible fossil beds and ancient sedimentary deposits from the Western Interior Seaway.

stateParks.name: Medicine Rocks State Park
stateParks.description: Sandstone formations riddled with holes and arches carved by wind erosion. The White River Formation sandstone contains unique weathering patterns and minor fossil deposits.

stateParks.name: Pictograph Cave State Park
stateParks.description: Sandstone caves with ancient pictographs. The Eagle Sandstone formations contain visible cross-bedding and ancient river deposit structures.

stateParks.name: Giant Springs State Park
stateParks.description: Features one of the largest freshwater springs in the US, emerging from Madison Limestone aquifer. Exposed limestone contains abundant marine fossils.

stateParks.name: Cooney State Park
stateParks.description: Reservoir surrounded by Beartooth Mountains geology — ancient Precambrian metamorphic rocks with visible igneous intrusions and mineralized zones.

stateParks.name: Hot Springs State Park
stateParks.description: World's largest mineral hot springs with travertine terraces formed by mineral-laden water. The park features colorful thermophile mineral deposits and a dinosaur museum nearby.

stateParks.name: Sinks Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: The Popo Agie River disappears into a limestone cave and resurfaces half a mile away. Dramatic canyon exposing Madison Limestone and Bighorn Dolomite.

stateParks.name: Boysen State Park
stateParks.description: Reservoir surrounded by spectacular Wind River Canyon geology — visible sedimentary layers spanning hundreds of millions of years of Earth history.

stateParks.name: Edness K. Wilkins State Park
stateParks.description: Along the North Platte River exposing Casper Sandstone formations. The area features visible fossil deposits and ancient river sedimentary structures.

stateParks.name: Seminoe State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic reservoir surrounded by Precambrian metamorphic and igneous rocks of the Seminoe Mountains. Visible quartz veins and mineralized zones.

stateParks.name: Keyhole State Park
stateParks.description: Reservoir exposing sedimentary rocks of the Powder River Basin. Visible coal deposits, sandstone cliffs, and ancient floodplain deposits.

stateParks.name: Hawk Springs State Recreation Area
stateParks.description: Reservoir in the High Plains exposing Tertiary-age sedimentary deposits. Visible fossiliferous sandstone and ancient stream channel deposits.

stateParks.name: Glendo State Park
stateParks.description: Reservoir carved through Triassic and Jurassic sedimentary rocks. Visible gypsum deposits, red bed formations, and fossil-bearing limestone layers.

stateParks.name: Massacre Rocks State Park
stateParks.description: Features dramatic basalt cliffs from the Snake River Plain volcanic activity. Visible columnar jointing and ancient Bonneville Flood scour marks.

stateParks.name: Malad Gorge State Park
stateParks.description: A 250-foot-deep basalt gorge carved by the Malad River. Exposes layered Snake River Plain basalt flows with visible interflow sedimentary deposits and fossil beds.

stateParks.name: Box Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: A spectacular spring-fed waterfall cascading into a basalt box canyon. Exposes Snake River Plain basalt formations and ancient flood deposits.

stateParks.name: Bruneau Dunes State Park
stateParks.description: Home to North America's tallest single-structured sand dune (470 feet). The dunes formed from sand eroded from surrounding basalt and sedimentary formations.

stateParks.name: Craters of the Moon (State Park adjacent)
stateParks.description: While primarily a National Monument, the adjacent state lands feature the same spectacular volcanic formations — lava tubes, cinder cones, and ropy pahoehoe basalt flows.

stateParks.name: Thousand Springs State Park
stateParks.description: Magnificent springs gushing from basalt canyon walls along the Snake River. The springs emerge from the Eastern Snake River Plain Aquifer through fractured basalt.

stateParks.name: Land of the Yankee Fork State Park
stateParks.description: Historic mining district with rich geology — visible quartz veins, mineralized zones, and abandoned mine workings in Challis Volcanic rocks.

stateParks.name: Heyburn State Park
stateParks.description: Idaho's oldest state park features exposed metamorphic rocks of the Belt Supergroup along Lake Coeur d'Alene. Visible quartzite and argillite formations.

stateParks.name: Steamboat Rock State Park
stateParks.description: A massive basalt mesa rising 800 feet above Banks Lake — a remnant of the Grand Coulee's Ice Age flood carving. Spectacular columnar jointing in basalt.

stateParks.name: Cape Disappointment State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic headland exposing Cape Disappointment conglomerate and volcanic basement rocks. The Columbia River bar geology and ancient beach deposits are visible.

stateParks.name: Palouse Falls State Park
stateParks.description: Washington's state waterfall drops 200 feet into a dramatic basalt canyon carved by Ice Age floods. Exposes layered Grand Ronde basalt flows of the Columbia River Basalt Group.

stateParks.name: Larrabee State Park
stateParks.description: Features dramatic Chuckanut Sandstone formations with visible tide pools and fossil leaf imprints. The sandstone contains Eocene-age plant fossils.

stateParks.name: Mount Spokane State Park
stateParks.description: Features exposed Precambrian metamorphic rocks of the Belt Supergroup. Visible quartzite, argillite, and dramatic geologic structures from ancient mountain building.

stateParks.name: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park
stateParks.description: Features Dry Falls — a 3.5-mile-wide ancient waterfall from Ice Age floods, now dry. Exposes massive basalt cliffs carved by the greatest known floods in Earth's history.

stateParks.name: Olive Stone / Beacon Rock State Park
stateParks.description: Beacon Rock is an 848-foot core of an ancient volcano — a massive basalt plug exposed by Ice Age floods. Spectacular geological formation along the Columbia River.

stateParks.name: Lewis & Clark Trail State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes basalt formations of the Blue Mountains foothills. Visible sedimentary interbeds between Columbia River Basalt flows contain fossil plant material.

stateParks.name: Chugach State Park
stateParks.description: Half-million acres of dramatic glacial carved terrain with exposed metamorphic schist, slate, and greywacke of the Chugach terrane. Visible glacial geology and fault structures.

stateParks.name: Kachemak Bay State Park
stateParks.description: Glaciers, fjords, and exposed sedimentary rock of the McNeil Formation with fossil-bearing strata. Tide pools reveal ancient marine sediments.

stateParks.name: Denali State Park
stateParks.description: Spectacular views of Denali with exposed Yukon-Tanana terrane metamorphic rocks including schist and quartzite. Glacial moraines and volcanic features.

stateParks.name: Crater of Diamonds State Park
stateParks.description: The only diamond-bearing site in the world open to public collecting. Diamonds formed in a 95-million-year-old volcanic pipe of lamproite. Keep what you find.

stateParks.name: Petit Jean State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic sandstone bluffs and Cedar Falls carving through Atoka Formation sandstone. Visible rock shelters with ancient pictographs.

stateParks.name: Mount Magazine State Park
stateParks.description: Arkansas's highest point at 2,753 feet. Exposed Pennsylvanian-age sandstone and shale of the Boston Mountain plateau.

stateParks.name: Sleeping Giant State Park
stateParks.description: Ridge of traprock (basalt) formed by Jurassic lava flows. The 'giant' profile is a classic example of columnar jointing in the Holyoke Basalt.

stateParks.name: West Rock Ridge State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic traprock ridge of West Rock basalt with columnar jointing. Overlooking New Haven with exposures of Jurassic lava flows.

stateParks.name: Trap Pond State Park
stateParks.description: Features wetlands over Columbia Formation gravel deposits. The surface geology reveals Pleistocene-age sediments from ancient coastal processes.

stateParks.name: Cape Henlopen State Park
stateParks.description: Atlantic barrier beach with dynamic dune geology. Exposes recent coastal sedimentary processes and the Peggy Island shell bed.

stateParks.name: Falling Waters State Park
stateParks.description: Florida's highest waterfall drops 73 feet into a cylindrical sinkhole. Exposes the Floridan aquifer limestone and karst dissolution features.

stateParks.name: Devil's Millhopper Geological State Park
stateParks.description: A 120-foot deep sinkhole exposing layers of limestone, sand, and clay from different geological eras. Fossil shark teeth and marine life found here.

stateParks.name: Rainbow Springs State Park
stateParks.description: First-magnitude spring discharging from the Floridan aquifer through limestone. Crystal clear water reveals the karst geology beneath.

stateParks.name: Providence Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: Georgia's 'Little Grand Canyon' — massive gullies carved by erosion in soft Coastal Plain sediments. A dramatic example of human-accelerated erosion.

stateParks.name: Amicalola Falls State Park
stateParks.description: 729-foot waterfall cascading over Blue Ridge metamorphic rocks. Exposes quartzite and schist of the Cartersville Dam area.

stateParks.name: Cloudland Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: Deep canyon carved into Sand Mountain exposing Pennsylvanian sandstone, shale, and coal seams. Dramatic overlooks of the Tennessee Valley.

stateParks.name: Akaka Falls State Park
stateParks.description: 442-foot waterfall plunging over basalt cliffs carved into ancient Mauna Kea lavas. Exposes layered Hawaiian volcanic flows.

stateParks.name: Waimea Canyon State Park
stateParks.description: The 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific' — 14 miles long and 3,600 feet deep, carved into the ancient volcanic rock of Kauai's Na Pali formation.

stateParks.name: Hāpuna Beach State Recreation Area
stateParks.description: White sand beach formed from coral and shell fragments over basalt. Reveals coastal volcanic geology of the Kohala coast.

stateParks.name: Maquoketa Caves State Park
stateParks.description: Limestone caves and karst features in Silurian-age dolomite. Contains stalactites, stalagmites, and solution caves typical of Iowa's driftless region.

stateParks.name: Ledges State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic sandstone cliffs carved by Pea's Creek into Pennsylvanian-age sandstone. Glacial erratics and loess deposits visible.

stateParks.name: Starved Rock State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic canyons carved into St. Peter Sandstone by glacial meltwater. 18 canyons expose Ordovician-age pure quartz sandstone.

stateParks.name: Giant City State Park
stateParks.description: Massive Pennsylvanian-age sandstone bluffs with giant 'city streets' — vertical jointing in the Caseyville Sandstone forms maze-like passages.

stateParks.name: Mississippi Palisades State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic limestone bluffs along the Mississippi River exposing Ordovician and Silurian dolomite. Fossil-bearing strata visible in cliff faces.

stateParks.name: Turkey Run State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic sandstone ravines carved into Pennsylvanian-age Mansfield Sandstone. Contains fossil plants and ancient coal measure geology.

stateParks.name: Brown County State Park
stateParks.description: Rugged terrain exposing Mississippian-age siltstone and shale of the Borden Group. Scenic ravines and weathered sandstone formations.

stateParks.name: McCormick's Creek State Park
stateParks.description: Indiana's oldest state park features limestone canyon carved by McCormick's Creek. Exposes Salem Limestone with abundant marine fossils.

stateParks.name: Mushroom Rock State Park
stateParks.description: Oddly shaped sandstone concretions resembling mushrooms. These Dakota Formation rocks are 100-million-year-old beach deposits with distinctive erosion forms.

stateParks.name: Monument Rocks (Chalk Pyramids)
stateParks.description: 70-foot chalk pinnacles and arches — remnants of the Niobrara Chalk Formation from the Western Interior Seaway. Rich in fossil marine reptiles and giant clams.

stateParks.name: El Capitan State Park / Mount Sunflower
stateParks.description: Kansas's highest point with exposures of Ogallala Formation calcareous sandstone and siltstone. Preserves High Plains geology.

stateParks.name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park
stateParks.description: 78-foot natural sandstone arch in the Red River Gorge Geological Area. Exposes Pennsylvanian-age Corbin Sandstone with dramatic cliff formations.

stateParks.name: Cumberland Falls State Resort Park
stateParks.description: 'Niagara of the South' — 125-foot wide waterfall over Pennsylvanian sandstone. Famous for moonbows. Exposes Coal Measures geology.

stateParks.name: Breaks Interstate Park
stateParks.description: 'Grand Canyon of the South' — 1,600-foot deep gorge carved by the Russell Fork through Pennsylvanian sandstone and shale. Dramatic cliff exposures.

stateParks.name: Lake Chicot State Park
stateParks.description: Ox-bow lake formed by the meandering Mississippi River. Exposes alluvial deposits and the Catahoula Formation with volcanic ash layers.

stateParks.name: Poverty Point State Historic Site
stateParks.description: UNESCO World Heritage earthworks built on loess deposits of the Mississippi River valley. The geology supported one of North America's oldest mound complexes.

stateParks.name: Mount Holyoke Range State Park
stateParks.description: Unique east-west traprock ridge of Jurassic basalt. Exposes the Holyoke Basalt with columnar jointing — part of the Connecticut Valley lava flows.

stateParks.name: Middlesex Fells Reservation
stateParks.description: Exposed Lynn Volcanics — rhyolite and tuff from the Precambrian Avalon terrane. Dramatic cliff formations and glacial erratics.

stateParks.name: Rocks State Park
stateParks.description: Features the King and Queen Seat — a 190-foot rock outcrop of Port Deposit gneiss. Exposes ancient Piedmont metamorphic rocks.

stateParks.name: Calvert Cliffs State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic cliffs along the Chesapeake Bay exposing Miocene marine sediments. World-famous for fossil shark teeth, whale bones, and shells.

stateParks.name: Assateague State Park
stateParks.description: Barrier island geology with dynamic dune systems. Exposes Pleistocene and Holocene coastal deposits and ancient beach processes.

stateParks.name: Baxter State Park
stateParks.description: Home to Mount Katahdin — a massive granite massif of Devonian age. Exposes Katahdin Granite and dramatic glacial cirques.

stateParks.name: Acadia National Park (Adjacent State Lands)
stateParks.description: Granite dome geology of the Cadillac Mountain Granite. Dramatic glacial carved coastline exposing pink Devonian granite.

stateParks.name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
stateParks.description: Ancient Precambrian basalt flows and conglomerate of the Keweenaw Peninsula. Exposes 1.1-billion-year-old Midcontinent Rift volcanic rocks.

stateParks.name: Tahquamenon Falls State Park
stateParks.description: Upper and lower falls carved into Cambrian Jacobsville Sandstone. The red rock is ancient stream-deposited sandstone.

stateParks.name: F.J. McLain State Park
stateParks.description: Keweenaw Peninsula basalt and conglomerate exposure. Native copper deposits occur in the Portage Lake Volcanics — historic copper mining geology.

stateParks.name: Gooseberry Falls State Park
stateParks.description: Waterfalls cascading over 1.1-billion-year-old basalt of the Midcontinent Rift. Exposes layered lava flows with columnar jointing.

stateParks.name: Tettegouche State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic Lake Superior shoreline exposing rhyolite and basalt of the North Shore Volcanic Group. High cliffs and waterfalls over volcanic rock.

stateParks.name: Interstate State Park
stateParks.description: Classic exposure of the Midcontinent Rift — basalt lava flows with glacial potholes carved into 1.1-billion-year-old rock.

stateParks.name: Elephant Rocks State Park
stateParks.description: Giant red granite boulders — Precambrian-age elephant-shaped rocks. Exposes 1.4-billion-year-old Butler Hill Granite with spectacular spheroidal weathering.

stateParks.name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
stateParks.description: River cascading over ancient rhyolite creating natural water slides. Exposes 1.4-billion-year-old Taum Sauk rhyolite of the St. Francois Mountains.

stateParks.name: Grand Gulf State Park
stateParks.description: 'Grand Canyon of the Ozarks' — collapsed cave system forming a mile-long gorge in Ordovician dolomite. Outstanding karst geology.

stateParks.name: Tupelo National Battlefield
stateParks.description: Exposes Selma Chalk Formation from the Late Cretaceous. Fossiliferous chalk deposits from the ancient Mississippi embayment.

stateParks.name: Red Bluff State Park / Clark Creek Natural Area
stateParks.description: Massive red clay and gravel exposure of the Citronelle Formation. Dramatic erosion gullies reveal Pliocene coastal plain geology.

stateParks.name: Mount Mitchell State Park
stateParks.description: Highest point east of the Mississippi at 6,684 feet. Exposes Precambrian gneiss and schist of the Blue Ridge Province.

stateParks.name: Hanging Rock State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic quartzite cliffs and waterfalls in the Sauratown Mountains. Exposes Precambrian quartzite of the Lynchburg Formation.

stateParks.name: Chimney Rock State Park
stateParks.description: 315-foot granite monolith overlooking Hickory Nut Gorge. Exposes Henderson Gneiss with dramatic glacial-era weathering features.

stateParks.name: Maah Daah Hey Trail / Theodore Roosevelt State Park
stateParks.description: Badlands topography exposing the Bullion Gap and Sentinel Butte Formations. Fossil-bearing Cretaceous and Paleocene strata with petrified wood.

stateParks.name: Fort Ransom State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Pierre Shale and Niobrara Formation chalks. Fossil ammonites and baculites found in the Cretaceous marine deposits.

stateParks.name: White Horse Hill State Park
stateParks.description: Glacial moraine geology along the shores of Devils Lake. Exposes Pleistocene till deposits and ancient glacial lake Agassiz sediments.

stateParks.name: Toadstool Geologic Park
stateParks.description: Badlands topography with bizarre 'toadstool' rock formations. Exposes Oligocene Brule and Chadron Formations with abundant mammal fossils.

stateParks.name: Ashfall Fossil Beds State Historical Park
stateParks.description: UNESCO site preserving rhinos and horses killed by a volcanic ash fall 12 million years ago. Exposes the Ash Hollow Formation with exceptional fossils.

stateParks.name: Smith Falls State Park
stateParks.description: Nebraska's highest waterfall over Tertiary-age Ogallala Formation sandstone. Exposes Pliocene river deposits.

stateParks.name: High Point State Park
stateParks.description: Highest point in New Jersey at 1,803 feet. Exposes Shawangunk Conglomerate — Silurian quartz pebble conglomerate with dramatic cliffs.

stateParks.name: Delaware Water Gap State Park Area
stateParks.description: Dramatic water gap cut through Kittatinny Ridge by the Delaware River. Exposes Silurian Shawangunk Formation quartzite.

stateParks.name: Letchworth State Park
stateParks.description: 'Grand Canyon of the East' — deep gorge carved by the Genesee River through Devonian shale and sandstone. Three major waterfalls expose Catskill Formation.

stateParks.name: Taughannock Falls State Park
stateParks.description: 215-foot waterfall — taller than Niagara — plunging over Devonian Tully Limestone into a hanging valley carved by glaciers.

stateParks.name: Minnewaska State Park Preserve
stateParks.description: Dramatic Shawangunk Conglomerate ridgeline with quartz pebble conglomerate cliffs. Exposes Silurian-age pure quartz sandstone.

stateParks.name: Hocking Hills State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic gorge and cave formations in Black Hand Sandstone. Exposes Mississippian-age sandstone with waterfalls carved into the resistant rock.

stateParks.name: John Bryan State Park
stateParks.description: Gorge cut by the Little Miami River through Silurian limestone and dolomite. Contains solution caves and spring-fed waterfalls.

stateParks.name: Caesar Creek State Park
stateParks.description: Emergency spillway exposes world-class Ordovician fossils — trilobites, brachiopods, and bryozoans in the rich fossil beds.

stateParks.name: Roman Nose State Park
stateParks.description: Canyon carved into red Permian sandstone and gypsum. Exposes the Dog Creek Shale and Blaine Formation with dramatic red rock cliffs.

stateParks.name: Robbers Cave State Park
stateParks.description: Sandstone cliffs and caves in the Savanna Formation. Exposes Pennsylvanian-age sandstone with dramatic rock shelters.

stateParks.name: Alabaster Caverns State Park
stateParks.description: Rare gypsum cave — the largest publicly accessible gypsum cave in the world. Exposes Permian-age Blaine Formation with selenite crystals.

stateParks.name: Ricketts Glen State Park
stateParks.description: 22 named waterfalls cascading over Pocono Formation sandstone and shale. Exposes Devonian and Mississippian age sedimentary rocks.

stateParks.name: Cook Forest State Park
stateParks.description: Ancient old-growth forest on Pottsville Sandstone ridges. Exposes Pennsylvanian-age sandstone with scenic rock formations.

stateParks.name: Leonard Harrison State Park
stateParks.description: 'Pennsylvania's Grand Canyon' overlook — 800-foot deep gorge carved by Pine Creek through Devonian sandstone and shale.

stateParks.name: Lincoln Woods State Park
stateParks.description: Exposed Rhode Island Formation metamorphic rocks — schist and quartzite of the Avalon terrane. Glacial erratics and polish visible.

stateParks.name: Colt State Park
stateParks.description: Coastal exposures of Rhode Island Formation sandstone and conglomerate. Scenic Narragansett Bay geology with glacial till deposits.

stateParks.name: Caesars Head State Park
stateParks.description: Granite escarpment overlooking the Blue Ridge Escarpment. Exposes Henderson Gneiss with dramatic 2,000-foot elevation change to the Piedmont.

stateParks.name: Table Rock State Park
stateParks.description: Iconic Table Rock granite dome of the Blue Ridge Province. Exposes Precambrian-age Henderson Gneiss with dramatic glacial-era weathering.

stateParks.name: Hunting Island State Park
stateParks.description: Barrier island with dynamic beach erosion exposing Pleistocene and Holocene coastal deposits. Fossil shark teeth occasionally found.

stateParks.name: Custer State Park
stateParks.description: Granite peaks of the Black Hills including Harney Peak granite. Exposes 1.7-billion-year-old Precambrian metamorphic and igneous rocks.

stateParks.name: Bear Butte State Park
stateParks.description: Geological laccolith — magma intrusion that pushed up sedimentary layers. Exposes phonolite porphyry similar to Devils Tower.

stateParks.name: Palisades State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic Sioux Quartzite cliffs along the Split Rock River. Exposes 1.6-billion-year-old pink quartzite — some of the oldest rock in South Dakota.

stateParks.name: Fall Creek Falls State Park
stateParks.description: 256-foot waterfall — one of the highest in the eastern US. Carved into Mississippian-age Monteagle Limestone with spectacular gorge geology.

stateParks.name: Cummins Falls State Park
stateParks.description: 75-foot waterfall into a deep gorge carved through Mississippian limestone. Rock pools and scenic waterfall geology.

stateParks.name: Pickett State Park
stateParks.description: Cumberland Plateau geology with natural arches and rock shelters in Pennsylvanian sandstone. Contains delicate sandstone formations.

stateParks.name: Natural Bridge State Park
stateParks.description: 215-foot natural limestone arch carved by Cedar Creek. A National Historic Landmark exposing Ordovician-age Beekmantown dolomite.

stateParks.name: Breaks Interstate Park
stateParks.description: 'Grand Canyon of the South' — 1,600-foot deep gorge through Pennsylvanian sandstone. Dramatic cliff exposures of the Russell Fork.

stateParks.name: Grayson Highlands State Park
stateParks.description: Highest point in Virginia with exposures of Mount Rogers rhyolite — some of the oldest volcanic rock in Virginia. Granitic intrusions visible.

stateParks.name: Smugglers' Notch State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic narrow pass between Mount Mansfield and Spruce Peak. Exposes Precambrian schist and quartzite of the Green Mountains.

stateParks.name: Quechee State Park
stateParks.description: Home to Vermont's deepest gorge — 165 feet deep — carved by the Ottauquechee River through Devonian quartzite and schist.

stateParks.name: Devil's Lake State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic 500-foot quartzite bluffs rising above a glacial lake. Exposes 1.7-billion-year-old Baraboo Quartzite — a classic Precambrian metamorphic rock.

stateParks.name: Parfrey's Glen State Natural Area
stateParks.description: Deep sandstone gorge carved through Cambrian-age sandstone. Wisconsin's first State Natural Area with delicate geological features.

stateParks.name: Lake Wissota State Park
stateParks.description: Glacial geology — the lake itself is a glacially carved basin. Exposes Cambrian sandstone and glacial drift deposits.

stateParks.name: New River Gorge State Park
stateParks.description: Deep gorge carved by one of the world's oldest rivers through Pennsylvanian sandstone and coal measures. Exposes Nuttall Sandstone cliffs.

stateParks.name: Hawks Nest State Park
stateParks.description: Overlooks the New River Gorge with exposures of Pennsylvanian-age sandstone and shale. Dramatic cliff geology of the Appalachian Plateau.

stateParks.name: Blackwater Falls State Park
stateParks.description: 62-foot waterfall over Pennsylvanian sandstone. Blackwater Canyon exposes Coal Measures and Pottsville Sandstone geology.

stateParks.name: Glendo State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Ogallala Formation conglomerates and Tertiary river deposits. Fossil wood found in the nearby White River Formation.

stateParks.name: Keyhole State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Spearfish Formation red shale and gypsum. Fossil-bearing Permian and Triassic sedimentary rocks visible in shoreline exposures.

stateParks.name: Little River Canyon National Preserve (State Park Access)

stateParks.name: Monte Sano State Park
stateParks.description: Mountain top exposing Mississippian-age Monteagle Limestone with fossil crinoids and brachiopods. Karst features and caves visible in the plateau geology.

stateParks.name: Gulf State Park
stateParks.description: Coastal barrier island geology exposing Pleistocene and Holocene beach deposits. Fossil shark teeth and shell beds occasionally exposed.

stateParks.name: Monadnock State Park
stateParks.description: Mount Monadnock — one of the world's most climbed mountains. Exposes Littleton Formation schist and quartzite, glacially polished metamorphic rock.

stateParks.name: Franconia Notch State Park
stateParks.description: Dramatic glacial notch exposing Littleton Formation schist and the famous Old Man of the Mountain granite cliff geology. Profile glacial cirque and Boise Rock exposures.

stateParks.name: Pawtuckaway State Park
stateParks.description: Exposes Pawtuckaway Complex igneous and metamorphic rocks. Dramatic glacial erratics and polished bedrock surfaces from the last ice age.
